lũa sa tùng, also sold as lũa kim sa tùng

lũa bonsai, and lũa xương chùm for its crown; and lũa xương trùm, as one shop writes it (no source says it is xương chùm)
lũa rễ rừng, and lũa thạch sùng with it

write: Boiling, said once, in one place: it is optional; it draws tannin from the outer layer faster; two keepers say it can make wood softer and quicker to rot, and no source says otherwise; for spider wood alone, a shop says it speeds sinking but can soften thin branches and break their tips. Sources differ on whether to boil at all (a keeper advises against it, since it can make wood rot faster; the shops advise it) and on whether it helps wood sink, never "sources differ only" on one of them: never "boiling does not make wood sink" as a plain fact, never softened branches for all wood, never "sources differ" on rot. Take out "Luộc không làm gỗ chìm, lại làm nhánh mảnh mềm đi, đầu nhánh dễ gãy." and "Các nguồn khác nhau ở chỗ luộc có làm lũa mau mục hay không."
Rot, said once, in one place: which wood lasts and the signs that a piece is rotting. Never "does not rot" beside "may be rotting".
Malaysian driftwood is mangrove root: write "rễ cây ngập mặn", never "đước".
Leave out: hydrogen peroxide and potassium permanganate, the Walstad remark, the 2,000 ppm of tannin, mopani's density and its percentages.
Cholla's item opens with what it is; the shops' sizes go last or out.
Lũa linh sam's own item says it sinks at once and what shops say of the colour it gives the water.
Lũa trà gừng and lũa xương trùm each keep an item of their own, apart from trà rừng and xương chùm, unless a source says they are the same wood.

Put back, where the facts give them, and grow nothing else: the white film peaks in weeks 1–2; only stainless screws, since other metals rust; wood too big for the tank takes the fish's swimming room; never put wood in while it still colours the water.
Manzanita: after the sources differ, say what to do, as the facts give it: soak it weighted for 3–4 weeks.
Malaysian driftwood has no Vietnamese name in the facts: never "lũa Malaysia".

Lũa vân thép and lũa thép: never "cũng mòn tới lõi như săn đá". One shop says "vân thép – san đá" is worn to the core; another calls lũa thép (vân thép) a newer, rough, very hard wood like linh sam. Give each only what its own source says.
Take the bucket line out of the kinds' opening paragraph: "Cách chắc nhất là ngâm thử trong xô, thấy nước hết ra màu rồi hãy cho vào bể." Soaking in a large bucket for 1–2 weeks stays where it is.
Boiling opens in the active voice: "Có thể luộc lũa trước khi dùng.", in place of "Lũa có thể được luộc trước khi dùng."
Grapevine goes back, in the one place rot is said: TFH Magazine says it breaks down fast under water and can set off bacteria, algae and fungus.

The kinds' opening paragraph keeps one line that weighs the shops' "không ra màu" against TFH Magazine's word that all wood gives off tannin, so the kinds whose shops say "không ra màu" have it beside them. The bucket line stays out.
One spelling: "biotope", never "BioTop": "bể BioTop nhiều gỗ ít cây" is "bể biotope nhiều gỗ ít cây".

Fish and plant names start in lower case mid-sentence in every sentence, those no other note touches too: "bể cá đĩa, cá ông tiên", "Anubias hay dương xỉ Java", "rêu Java hay dương xỉ Java", "bể cá betta (cá xiêm) hay cá bảy màu". A proper name in them keeps its capital (Java).
Mopani: take out "Ở Việt Nam, mopani của Zoo Med được bán dưới tên "Gỗ lũa cho bể cá Zoo Med Mopani"." A glossary names no brand and no shop listing's title: say only that a shop in Vietnam sells it.

length.why: The nitrogen cycle's facts hold an emergency exception, the nitrite test's unit and a tap-water check that take its entry past 400. The chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026: 450, then 480 once every read sentence was kept (about 476 words whole); a cap that makes the writer cut a caution is the wrong cap.

also: whether keeping tap water for some days or aerating it removes chloramine as well as chlorine, and what to use when tap water carries chloramine
write: Planting before the cycle is stable is not a mistake: one shop says it can rot roots, and AquaTome's own cycling guides plant first and then cycle. Keep the fish half, in the mistakes list, and say there that the fish can die: fish added during the ammonia stage fall ill easily (very prone to disease then) and can die (a shop: adding fish before the cycle is stable can lead to fish deaths). Say it once, there.

Tap water is dechlorinated with a dechlorinator, "thuốc khử clo", named by its kind, never by a brand: the kind that also handles chloramine (the vet source: a dechlorinator designed for chloramines that also binds the ammonia they release). Not Seachem Prime or any other product by name.

The filter is mature when TAN and nitrite peak and then fall to 0 or near 0 (a shop: test readings drop to or near 0), and then nitrate rises (the vet source: they peak and fall, followed by a rise in nitrate). Give "0 hoặc gần 0" once, in that sentence.

How long the cycle takes is one statement, never a shop set against the vet source (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026): a new filter usually takes about 6 weeks to be fully established (the vet source); bacteria added regularly, or water and filter media from a healthy established tank, make it shorter (the shops: about 2 weeks with supplements, 3–7 days with used media). For example "Lọc mới thường mất khoảng 6 tuần mới ổn định hẳn, nhanh hơn nếu có vi sinh hay vật liệu lọc từ bể cũ." How a keeper knows it is done is already the daily TAN and nitrite test in the steps and the filter-mature sentence: don't repeat it here. Never say that 1–2 weeks is too early: the facts don't say it, and a seeded filter can be done by then (the fact check, Mon 16 Nov).

The emergency water change keeps the vet source's exception, in the same place: when ammonia is high, change at least 50% of the water at once and cut feeding; and when TAN is above 5 mg/L and pH is below 7, move the fish to clean water at the same temperature, since otherwise, as the pH rises, that ammonia turns quickly to toxic NH3 (the vet source; a shop: below pH 7 more of it is the less harmful NH4+). Say it in those terms only: the facts don't say "instead of a water change", nor that a water change raises pH or is the wrong move, so don't say either.

The nitrite line says which reading its 0,1 is, so a keeper compares like with like: toxic from about 0,1 mg/L counted as NO2; some test kits read nitrite as nitrite-nitrogen (the vet source says most, but the drop kits sold here read NO2, the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026), and on such a kit that is about 0,03, since the kit's reading times 3,3 gives NO2 (the vet source). "Một số bộ test", never "đa số".

Beside the emergency change, check whether the tap water carries ammonia or chloramine, since water changes can bring ammonia in (the vet source). Say it once, there, with no order: the facts don't say to check first, and they say to change the water as soon as high ammonia is found.

If it can be said naturally in this run: the dechlorinator's clause in a keeper's Vietnamese, not word for word from the English "binds the released ammonia" (now "giữ lại amoniac mà nó nhả ra"), for example "…loại khử được cả chloramine và khóa luôn lượng amoniac sinh ra". The facts as they are; nothing else in that sentence changes.

Keep the seeding sentence as it stands, word for word: "Châm thêm men vi sinh của hãng uy tín, hoặc lấy nước, bông lọc từ một bể đã ổn định; riêng vật liệu lọc thì chỉ lấy từ bể đã ổn định mà cá trong đó đều khỏe." (the vet source: commercial nitrifying bacteria from a reputable source; two shops: water and floss from an established tank, media only from one whose fish are all healthy). Never the bottled bacteria alone.

Keep the daily test while the filter cycles, once, as the vet source gives it: test TAN and nitrite every day, with frequent water changes, until the filter has matured ("Đo TAN và nitrit mỗi ngày, thay nước thường xuyên cho tới khi lọc chín."). A trim for length never takes it out.
free: Có tiệm nói chu trình xong sau 1–2 tuần, nhưng tài liệu thú y ghi rằng lọc mới thường mất khoảng 6 tuần mới ổn định hẳn.
Đa số bộ test lại đọc nitrit

also: how far dry Indian almond leaves lower pH, and whether they lower it less in hard or well-buffered (high KH) water, from a page that gives a figure

length.why: pH's facts hold the scale, the tank's range, raising and lowering it by each method with its caution and pace, and how it moves ammonia: more than 400 words carry. The chief of staff: 600 on 14 Nov 2026, then 620 on 15 Nov once every read sentence was kept (about 615 words whole); a cap that makes the writer cut a caution is the wrong cap. Then 630 on Wed 18 Nov: the almond-leaf credit and the pace in its step leave it at about 620, and at 620 the writer cut whole sentences and the drop check stopped every rewrite (the Glossary lead, on the chief of staff's same rule; the chief of staff: "the 630 cap fine", Wed 18 Nov).

write: Leave out lowering pH to about 6.0–6.5 during ammonia poisoning: no source gives a pace for that case, and it stood a few lines above "changing pH too fast can kill fish". The water change for ammonia poisoning is 50% of the water, the one figure this entry and the nitrogen cycle's share, since two entries can't disagree on an emergency (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026): the vet page here gives 25–50% (source 1) and the vet manual behind the nitrogen cycle at least 50%, so 50% stands in both. For example "Khi cá ngộ độc amoniac, thay 50% nước."

No acid anywhere in this entry: its caution doesn't fit in 600 words. Where pH is high, the point is restraint, said within the facts: find and take out what is raising pH (coral, limestone, shells and the like) before adding anything to lower it (a shop); and if the source water is below 8 but the tank is higher, something in the tank is raising it (a shop). Not "Nước nguồn pH 8 thì mới đáng chỉnh." or any line on source water at pH 8: without the acid that shop spoke of, the fact check reads it as unsupported. Nothing on corrections wearing off after hours or a day, which the source says of acid.

The meaning's line on steadiness gives both halves, each as its source says it, so there is nothing loose to tighten: in a stable tank there is no need to worry much about the exact pH (a shop); what to avoid is a sudden change (a fish-care page: sudden or drastic pH changes can harm or even kill fish). For example "Bể đã ổn định thì không cần quá bận tâm đến con số pH chính xác; điều cần tránh là pH đổi đột ngột." Never the first half alone. It is not a repeat of the mistakes line on changing pH too fast, which says how.

The meaning names examples, as the facts give them: cá neon vua (cardinal tetra) lives in water below pH 5.5, and the Rift Lake cichlids prefer pH 8.0–9.0, written "cichlid hồ châu Phi" as it was, never "cichlid Rift Lake". Never "có loài… có loài…".

Keep these as specific as the facts carry them: test tap water or well water ("nước máy hoặc nước giếng"; a page names both as source water); change about 20–30% of the water weekly with treated, tested water (one page); below pH 7.3 more of the ammonia is the less harmful ammonium NH4+ (the source compares: "more of it", never "mostly"), said in words a keeper would use, as "Dưới 7,3 thì dạng amoni NH4+ ít hại hơn chiếm nhiều hơn"; never "phần nhiều hơn của nó", never "chủ yếu".

Coral is said once, as a trade-off, where it is first advised for raising low pH (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026): crushed coral or shells raise pH (a vet page), and coral also raises GH and TDS, which are hard to control (a shop). No "a shop says" and no second line on coral after it. Never say coral or shells go in "từng ít một" as if a source said it of them, and never "Đừng dùng san hô" or any plain "don't" on coral.

The pace for raising pH is the slower one the facts carry, since a source in them gives it (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026): no more than 0,2 a day (source 6; source 1 gives 0,5), whatever is used, with a test after. It is said once, in the low-pH step, right after the coral trade-off, word for word "Dùng thứ nào thì cũng nâng pH từ từ, mỗi ngày không quá 0,2 đơn vị, rồi đo lại." It never moves to the mistakes list, and the mistake "Chỉnh pH quá nhanh" doesn't repeat it (a Sonnet reader, Wed 18 Nov: the baking soda step lost its pace when it moved).

The weekly water change keeps its reason: about 20–30% of the water weekly with treated, tested water (one page), which also brings back the minerals that buffer pH (a fish-care page: regular partial water changes replace the minerals that buffer pH).

The mistakes list keeps the caution as a fish-care page gives it, whatever else is trimmed for length: sudden or drastic pH changes can harm or even kill fish. "pH đổi đột ngột có thể làm cá chết." stays with "Chỉnh pH quá nhanh.".

The log scale keeps its worked example, as a fish-care page gives it: pH 4.0 is ten times as acidic as pH 5.0 and a hundred times as acidic as pH 6.0 ("Mỗi nấc cách nhau 10 lần, tức là pH 4,0 chua gấp 10 lần pH 5,0 và gấp 100 lần pH 6,0."). A trim for length never takes it out.
Nothing on alum (phèn chua), not even as a mistake (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026): the one fact on it, that alum doesn't lower pH, is wrong, and no fact gives a true reason against it.

CO2's limit is said as what it is (the chief of staff, Sun 15 Nov 2026, 11:21): a cap on how far pH may fall while the CO2 runs, measured from the reading taken before it is switched on: test every 30 minutes and turn the CO2 off ("tắt CO2") at about 1 unit below that reading (source 4: stop at about 1 unit below the baseline; a drop of 0.7–1 unit is safe; source 2: swings are bigger with added CO2). It is not a way to bring the tank's pH down, so never "Nếu dùng CO2 để hạ pH…", and it sits apart from the 0,2-a-day pace, which is for moving the tank's pH. For example "Khi châm CO2, pH tụt trong lúc CO2 chạy: ghi pH trước khi bật, đo 30 phút một lần và tắt CO2 khi pH đã thấp hơn mức đó khoảng 1 đơn vị." If the facts can't carry this, CO2 stays only in the list of what lowers pH, with no method.

Indian almond leaves, as their facts give it (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026, in place of the Sun 15 Nov line). The item opens as it stands, "Lá bàng và lũa: tanin trong chúng làm pH xuống." (facts 31, 45, 48: several pages). How far is one shop's page alone (facts 81, 82, 83, source 8), so it goes under that shop's opening, with no place: those facts don't name one (the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov 2026: a claim only one page makes says whose it is; the place goes in a credit only when a fact under it names the place). That they lower it slowly is another shop's alone (fact 46, source 4), and the opening already says they lower it, so it goes: never "Lá bàng hạ pH chậm." (a Sonnet reader, Wed 18 Nov). Word for word: "Lá bàng và lũa: tanin trong chúng làm pH xuống. Một tiệm ghi: trong nước mềm, lá bàng hạ pH khoảng 0,2–0,5 đơn vị, còn ở nước cứng, đệm tốt thì gần như không đổi."
The electronic pen names what it is more accurate than, as the page says: litmus paper (source 6), "chính xác hơn giấy quỳ" (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026).
free: Nếu dùng CO2 để hạ pH, ghi lại pH trước khi bật CO2, đo 30 phút một lần trong lúc chạy và dừng khi pH thấp hơn mức ban đầu khoảng 1 đơn vị.
có thể tới khoảng 1–2 đơn vị
còn ở nước có KH trên 4–5 thì gần như không đổi
Lá bàng hạ pH chậm.
Khi nâng pH, dùng thứ nào cũng chỉ nâng mỗi ngày không quá 0,2 đơn vị, rồi đo lại.

write: The drop test is API's kit, as facts 29 and 30 give it, in one statement with its steps: rinse the tube with tank water, fill it to the 5 mL mark, add the reagent a drop at a time, shaking after each, until the colour turns from orange to green; the number of drops is the dGH. As in "Với bộ test GH nhỏ giọt của API, tráng ống bằng nước bể, đổ nước bể tới vạch 5 mL rồi nhỏ thuốc từng giọt, mỗi giọt lắc một lần, cho tới khi nước đổi từ cam sang xanh lá. Số giọt là số dGH." (the Sonnet reader, Tue 17 Nov: the facts give no other kit's steps, so my Monday line asking for a general drop test went past them).

Lowering GH carries its pace, as a shop gives it: lower it gradually, with small water changes, so the tank softens over time. RO water is named once, in the first sentence on lowering GH, not again here.

Which fish want which water, as the live entry has it and two sources give it (sources 1 and 2): soft-water fish such as cá đĩa want GH at 3 dGH or below, while cá đẻ con, cá vàng and cichlid hồ châu Phi want it higher. Not the one source's 1–17 dGH "fine for all adult fish", never "cá lớn": beside the soft-water fish it reads as if any GH will do (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026).

Shrimp's stability in a keeper's Vietnamese, not word for word from the English "above almost everything else" (now "sự ổn định được đặt lên trên gần như mọi thứ khác"), keeping its "almost" (a keeper's page: stability above almost everything else), as "Với tép, giữ nước ổn định quan trọng hơn gần như mọi thứ khác." (the chief of staff's wording, 15 Nov 2026)
What GH measures is said once, in the definition. The body's first section opens with the unit and the scales, not "GH đếm các ion canxi và magie trong nước."
Other names are only names Vietnamese keepers use for GH, as the facts write them: "độ cứng chung", "độ cứng tổng". "dGH" is the unit, not a name for GH, so it is not among them.

One hardness scale across GH, nước mềm and nước cứng, as those two entries give it: nước mềm under 6 dGH, 6 to 12 dGH between, nước cứng from 12 dGH (source 7's scale; its "very hard" is the hard water of Nước cứng). Never "rất cứng". Write the words "nước mềm" and "nước cứng" in that sentence: the site links each to its entry (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026).
The three stones stay, each named by a fact as limestone that raises GH: đá kẹp kem, đá da voi and đá tai mèo (source 5; đá kẹp kem also source 3).
No "Ví dụ" before API's kit and no second sentence on it: it is the only kit the facts give, so there is nothing general for it to be an example of (the Sonnet reader, Tue 17 Nov).

Eggs, larvae and fry are more sensitive to GH than adults, said with the rest of its fact, the range tied to them: "…, nhưng với chúng, các nhà nghiên cứu vẫn thấy một khoảng rộng là ổn, thường 20–300 ppm" (fact 11). Never the first half alone, and never a bare "một khoảng rộng" right after the discus line, where it reads as the discus' range (the Sonnet reader, Mon 16 Nov).
Discus need water with GH at 3 dGH (50 ppm) or below: "cần nước có GH từ 3 dGH (50 ppm) trở xuống", not "cần GH hạ xuống … trở xuống".
RO water is said once, in the first sentence on lowering GH; the pace sentence keeps only the pace: lower it slowly, with small water changes, so the tank softens over time (fact 41).

The low-GH sentence says what its facts say and no more, shrimp and snails each in their own clause: too low GH can leave shrimp with a soft shell they struggle to break out of when they molt (facts 20 and 22), and snail shells thin, flaking or pitted (fact 20), as in "GH quá thấp có thể làm vỏ tép mềm, tép khó thoát ra khỏi vỏ khi lột, còn vỏ ốc thì mỏng, bong hoặc rỗ." Never "làm … khó" without "có thể", and never "vỏ mới mềm" (Mon 16 Nov: an earlier line here asked for both, beyond its facts).

1 dGH is 17,9 ppm (mg/L) counted as calcium carbonate (fact 2), in the words Vietnam's water standard uses (fact 56): "1 dGH bằng 17,9 ppm (mg/L) tính theo CaCO3". Never 17,9 ppm bare (the Sonnet reader, Mon 16 Nov).
Lowering GH with a cation exchanger, as its fact names it (fact 38): "chất trao đổi cation", with no form the fact doesn't give, such as "hạt" (the Sonnet reader, Mon 16 Nov).

The meaning gives the minerals' uses as its facts do: shrimp molting, snail shells, fish bones and plant growth (fact 6), so "cá cần để lên xương", fish in general, not "cá con" alone (the Sonnet reader, Tue 17 Nov).
free: GH đếm các ion canxi và magie trong nước.
sự ổn định được đặt lên trên gần như mọi thứ khác
Cá lớn chịu được GH dao động rộng, từ 1 dGH (20 ppm) đến 17 dGH (300 ppm) đều ổn.
và pha thêm nước RO
Với bộ test GH nhỏ giọt của API, tráng ống bằng nước bể, đổ nước bể tới vạch rồi nhỏ thuốc từng giọt, mỗi giọt lắc một lần, và đếm số giọt cho tới khi nước đổi màu.
Ví dụ, với bộ test GH của API, ống đổ tới vạch 5 mL, nước đổi từ cam sang xanh lá, và số giọt là số dGH.

length.why: Steps: the drip test (rinse, fill to 5 mL, a drop at a time until orange turns green) and the coral dose to raise GH. The chief of staff's rule, 15 Nov 2026: 500 for a term whose facts carry steps a keeper follows or a set of forms, about 400 for any other.

write: Bloodworms are never thawed in hot water (facts 49, 66, 67: three pages), said of bloodworms, with no credit (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov; second pages from research, Wed 18 Nov).

Betta is "cá betta", the site's spelling, wherever the fish is meant. The bloodworm item reads word for word "Tiệm thứ nhất cũng ghi: loại này hợp với cá ăn thịt như cá betta." (the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov, on the 09:24 reader). Never "như Betta".

Each warning once, in one place: the freezer door in the storage step only; overfeeding in the mistakes list only, where it fouls the water (facts 48, 51, 61) and, with bloodworms, can bloat the fish (48, 69, 70), all with no credit; the feeding step gives the amount alone. "Vốn nhiều năng lượng" goes (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov; second pages from research, Wed 18 Nov).

The kinds sold in Vietnam with a line or two each: trùng huyết, artemia, trùn chỉ. Bobo (facts 20, 63) and tim bò (19, 64) are each sold by two Vietnamese shops: named together in one sentence with no credit, as in "Tiệm ở Việt Nam còn bán bobo và tim bò đông lạnh." Lăng quăng (18) found no second shop and goes (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov; second pages from research, Wed 18 Nov).

Thawing in one place, the two ways. Thawed apart in a small cup of tank water and rinsed (facts 25, 26, 27, 28: no credit). Throwing the thaw water away is the Singapore shop's alone (fact 27; fact 26 pours its soak water in), so it goes under that shop's credit in the form reading order gives it, as in "Cách thứ hai là rã riêng một phần mồi trong cốc nhỏ nước bể vài phút, tráng mồi rồi cho ăn. Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi: đổ bỏ nước rã đông." (the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov, 07:5x, on the reader). Why it is thrown away (fact 45) goes. Straight into the tank (fact 24): one shop gives it as an ordinary way, and another counts it a mistake (fact 44, one fact holding both): say that the two shops differ, once, never one as the rule (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov; the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov, 06:54)

The general feeding step: what the fish finish within a few minutes ("trong vài phút"): the pages give 2–3 minutes (fact 30) and, for bloodworm, 3–5 (fact 31), so neither figure stands alone. About half a cube a meal for a 60–90 litre community tank is one shop's (fact 30), said as that shop's (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov).

Feeding said once, as most of the facts give it: once or twice a day, what the fish finish in a few minutes, with the range the line on how much at a meal gives (never 2–5 minutes alone as the rule), and scraps taken out right away. Goldfish is "cá vàng"; the Latin name only beside it, as "cá vàng (Carassius)", never alone.

The complete food's nutrients and its daily feeding stand in the makers' one sentence (the line on "Đầy đủ dinh dưỡng"): its "để" is the makers' own join, as facts 56 and 58 each give both in one fact. Never "nên" (the second standing line; the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov).

(facts 23–26), never "khoảng từ hai phút trở xuống tới 5 phút" and never "dưới 2 phút" (the Sonnet reader; the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov, 07:5x); the betta line is word for word "Một nguồn người nuôi ghi: cá betta mỗi lần ăn 2–4 viên, ngày một hai lần.", never "chỉ cần" (the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov, 06:49; the Writing Lead, Wed 18 Nov).

also: The colour of decapsulated (shell-less) dried brine shrimp eggs as sold to feed fish (Vietnamese shops: "Artemia tách vỏ sấy khô"; English: "Decapsulated Brine Shrimp Eggs"), as a page states it in words. Where no page you may use states a colour, add nothing (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov: the generated stand-in waits on this fact)

A page that shows a photo of decapsulated dried brine shrimp eggs, on Wikimedia Commons, Openverse, Aquarium Co-op, Seriously Fish, 2Hr Aquarist, Aquarium Breeder or ScotCat: one fact naming the page and what its photo shows, in the page's own words. Never a shop's sale page or a marketplace (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov: a real photo beats the stand-in)
write: The meaning's first sentence says what Artemia is, in one clause: "giáp xác nhỏ sống ở nước mặn" (the top-up's reference page: a genus of small aquatic crustaceans, found worldwide, typically in inland saltwater lakes; "loài" is left out, since Artemia is a genus); then what a keeper does with it: eggs hatched in salt water into larvae, a live food for fry, small fish and shrimp. The English name comes after, never as the first sentence (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026).
No line saying sources differ: not "Các nguồn ghi lượng muối khác nhau." The next sentence gives both amounts, and that is enough.

Other names only as the facts give them for the whole term: the English "brine shrimp". "ấu trùng Artemia" names only the newly hatched larvae (source 3): it stays in the text for them, not among the other names.
Too much air sticks the eggs to the jar above the water line (source 0): "dính lên thành bình, phía trên mực nước", never "nằm trên mặt nước".
The eggs' amount as the shops give it, with the ceiling apart: about 1 g a litre (source 3), no more than 5 g a litre (source 0); too many eggs or too few lowers the hatch rate (source 2).

Salt: one working figure, then the range once, in the same sentence, with no one named in the text: about 30 g of non-iodized salt a litre (sources 3 and 9), and recipes run from about 5 g a litre up to that (source 0: 10–20 g in 2 litres; sources 1 and 2 between). Who said which lives in the sources, never "hai tiệm… một hội cá cảnh"; never "muối ăn" (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026).

When the air goes off: the shells float and the larvae gather lower down, drawn to a light (sources 0 and 3). Where the unhatched eggs go, the sources don't agree (source 0: they float; source 3: they sink), so the steps don't say. They say how to keep both out of the fry tank wherever they lie: gather the larvae with a light, siphon them from there and pour them through the fine net. The mistakes list keeps its warning (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026).
Decapsulated eggs, once, in their item: eggs that sink to the bottom are wasted and foul the water (source 7), and fresh ones may sink too fast for fry that don't feed off the bottom (source 8).

Harvest timing as one statement: turn the air off, wait about 5 minutes, and siphon before 10, when the oxygen runs short and the larvae start to die (source 0). Never "chờ 5–10 phút" beside the 10 minutes (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026).

Sinh khối Vĩnh Châu goes, with the shop's advice: no fact says what sinh khối is, and the one fact is a shop's sale line for Betta fry (source 5), which grown Artemia are far too big for (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026). The forms are the eggs and the decapsulated eggs.

The forms' item names stay as they are written, "Trứng Artemia" and "Artemia tách vỏ sấy khô", under a heading that opens "Các dạng": each name is the id Curation files a picture under (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026).
Light while hatching, once, in the step that sets the jar up: keep the jar lit for the first 24 hours (source 3).

Feeding, as the facts give it: in the salt water the larvae are richest in their first 12 hours after hatching, so they are harvested and fed within that (source 2). Feeding "a little at a time" is the decapsulated eggs' advice, not the live larvae's.

The air line in the order a keeper reads it: "Thả dây oxy xuống sát đáy bình, không gắn đá sủi" (source 0: an airline without an airstone, near the bottom), not "Cắm dây oxy không gắn cục sủi sát đáy bình" (the chief of staff, 15 Nov 2026).

The eggs' item ("Trứng Artemia") names Vĩnh Châu in one clause, with no item of its own, as its fact gives it: Artemia was brought to the salt fields of Vĩnh Châu in the early 1980s, since Vietnam had none of its own (the WAS magazine page), as in "Ở Việt Nam, Artemia được đưa về ruộng muối Vĩnh Châu từ đầu thập niên 1980, vì nước ta vốn không có Artemia." Not that every egg farmed here comes from Vĩnh Châu: farming has spread to other salt fields in the Mekong Delta. Nothing on their quality, size, hatch rate, price, or how much of what is sold here is imported: the pages that say it give no measure, or their figures disagree.

"Ấu trùng đã sang giai đoạn thứ hai cũng khó cho cá bột bắt hơn." stays, word for word, beside the 12-hour sentence (fact: second-instar larvae are harder for fry to catch). A run from the kept draft dropped it on Mon 16 Nov without leave: write it back.

The decapsulated eggs' size and what it suits, in one sentence, as fact 44 gives it: dried eggs are smaller than the larvae, so they suit smaller fish, as in "Hạt trứng khô nhỏ hơn ấu trùng nên hợp với cá nhỏ hơn." Never the comparison in one sentence and "hợp với cá miệng nhỏ hơn" two sentences on (the Sonnet reader, Mon 16 Nov).

With the shell gone, every egg, hatched or not, can be fed (fact 43): "mọi hạt trứng, nở hay không, đều cho ăn được", never "cá con ăn được hết", which reads as any fry can eat it (the Sonnet reader, Mon 16 Nov).

write: Nền bể is the bottom layer of a tank as a whole: what it is for, then the kinds shops here sell, each a line or two, since each kind's picture shows how it looks. Nền cát has its own entry: link it, and don't repeat what it says.

Each kind's first sentence says what it looks like, as its facts give it: grain or piece size, shape, colour, how it sits on the tank floor. A card on the term page shows that sentence alone beside the kind's photo, or in words where there is no photo, so it can never be a shop's note on its use (the Design Lead's board, 16 Nov 2026: "loại hay dùng nhất để set bố cục" says nothing of its look). What it's for comes after, in the kind's next sentences. A kind whose look no fact gives says that plainly in its first sentence, in a keeper's words, such as "Chưa có nguồn nào tả … trông thế nào.": never the word "dữ kiện" or any other word of ours about how the entry is made (Mon 16 Nov: four kinds opened on "dữ kiện chưa tả").

Xỉ than's item carries its fact's advice with its warnings, never a warning alone (Rule 9): rinse it very well before use; its iron oxide can tint the water orange and feed algae, it can raise hardness, and badly made slag may hold heavy metals (one fact, Mon 16 Nov; the checker stopped the draft that left the rinse out).

Cốt nền's look is said for the kinds its facts describe, never for every cốt nền: one sold here is brown grains of 1–3 mm, another looks like lava rock ("có loại …, có loại …"); no product named. Its use follows: laid under sand or phân nền (Mon 16 Nov top-up, read against its pages).

Akadama's look is what every grade shares: porous clay grains, earth-coloured, darker when wet (its facts: a clay fired for bonsai; porous granules; it darkens when moist). Its size is said as grades: it is sold in several grain sizes, and softer grades can crumble (the encyclopedia). Never "1–4 mm" or "cứng" for all akadama: those are one product's and one grade's (Mon 16 Nov read-back).

Each kind's other names come last in its item, after its look, whether it sinks, what it does to the water and what it is for (Rule 7): nham thạch trắng's "đá lông vũ, đá bọt biển" go at the end of its item.

Black patches or a rotten-egg smell (the sign of airless pockets) is said once, joined to its cause and what to do, never the sign alone (Rule 9): sand packed too tight forms them, so use a thinner layer, keep bottom fish that sift it, or stir it by hand (the sand facts). The sifting is the fish's, never the keeper's: "nuôi cá đáy biết sàng cát", not "nuôi cá đáy hay sàng cát" (the Sonnet reader, Mon 16 Nov).

Hold it to 580 by taking out these two free sentences: "Nền có thể nhả chất vào nước hoặc hút chất từ nước." and "Vi khuẩn có lợi bám lên nền mà sinh sôi, góp phần lọc sinh học cho bể." (the meaning and lava's item say both). Nothing else is cut: every kind keeps its look sentence, lava keeps how it is laid, and the plants' sentence stays.

The plants' sentence stays, word for word as follows, with no plant named but Vallisneria: "Cây trồng cắm rễ vào nền, và có loài như Vallisneria lấy thức ăn chủ yếu qua rễ." (fact 3). No other plant's name, and no clause added to it (the chief of staff, Mon 16 Nov: free to rewrite, not to cut; "cỏ lươn" and "Bleherae" come from no fact).
Packed sand can form airless pockets (fact 63: "can form"): "có thể sinh ra túi yếm khí", never "sẽ" (Mon 16 Nov).
Peat moss's look as fact 102 gives it, in a keeper's words: "vật liệu dạng sợi màu nâu", not "chất sợi" (the Sonnet reader, Mon 16 Nov).
Lava's pores, where helpful bacteria live (fact 79), are their own sentence after how it is laid, never joined to it by a comma (the Sonnet reader, Mon 16 Nov).

The root-tab sentence says only what its fact gives (fact 29: add root tabs after one or two years), with "phân nhét" once and no place the fact doesn't give, as "Lúc đó bổ sung phân nhét." (the chief of staff, Mon 16 Nov: "gần rễ cây" is free).

Three pages keep a credit, each with one opening carrying all its claims, and no other page is named. The 24–48-hour shop, "Một tiệm ghi …": soaking 24–48 hours in dechlorinated water for a lighter first tint (fact 25); in a shrimp tank, leaves can stay until only the skeleton is left (fact 28); leaves from busy roadsides can carry exhaust (fact 37). length.why: Steps a keeper follows: how many leaves, how to prepare them, when to replace them. The chief of staff's rule, 15 Nov 2026: 500 for a term whose facts carry steps or a set of forms. 550 from Wed 18 Nov: its draft holds every fix at 543 words, and a trim of a draft past its length can cut only the new words, the fixes (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov).

write: A flow figure keeps its unit as its fact gives it (how many times the tank's volume a filter moves in an hour, "lần thể tích bể mỗi giờ"). One page's figure says whose it is (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov 2026).

A fish's need for strong or gentle flow is said of the fish its fact names, by the site's own name with its kind word ("cá betta", "cá đĩa", "cá chạch suối"). It is never carried to a group the fact doesn't name (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov 2026).

Flow and aeration are two things: "dòng chảy" is the water's movement, "sục khí" adds air. A sentence joins them only where a fact does (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov 2026).

The definition's line on stream fish needing "nhiều oxy" stays only if a fact gives it. Oxy hòa tan's entry is linked for the oxygen itself (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov 2026).

Sewellia lineolata is named by its Latin name, with what its fact says of it, a stream fish native to Vietnam, under Seriously Fish's name, which the fact gives (fact 56). Word for word: "Trang Seriously Fish ghi: Sewellia lineolata, một loài cá suối có ở Việt Nam, cần dòng mạnh và nước nhiều oxy; lọc cho loài này tốt nhất là đảo nước 15–20 lần thể tích bể mỗi giờ." Never "loài chạch suối", "cá tỳ bà bướm hổ" or any Vietnamese name for it: no fact gives one, and the fact check stops a name it can't find (a Sonnet reader; the Glossary lead, Wed 18 Nov).

The signs of too strong a flow are the first shop's alone for fish in general (fact 15; fact 17 is about bettas only), so they open that shop's credit, word for word: "Một tiệm ghi: khi dòng quá mạnh, cá phải bơi ngược dòng liên tục, đuôi bị cuốn đi, hoặc nép vào một góc bể." The shop's next claim then opens "Tiệm thứ nhất cũng ghi: lưu lượng thật giảm 20–30% …". Never the signs written plain, never "nhìn cá là biết", and being swept adrift is the betta page's alone (fact 17) (the third Sonnet reader; the Glossary lead, Wed 18 Nov).

Units as the site writes them, metric only: the flow rate is "L/h" or how many times the tank's volume an hour (facts 1, 2), word for word "Lưu lượng của lọc ghi bằng L/h, hay bằng số lần thể tích bể mỗi giờ." Never "GPH" (a Sonnet reader; the Glossary lead, Wed 18 Nov).

The credited pages read the same in every entry: the first shop (Thủy Sinh 24, source 1) is first "Một tiệm ghi:", at the signs of too strong a flow, then "Tiệm thứ nhất cũng ghi:"; the second shop (source 2) is first "Một tiệm khác ghi:", then "Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi:"; Seriously Fish is named, "Trang Seriously Fish ghi:". Never "Cũng tiệm đó", "Tiệm này", "Tiệm cũng" or "Một tài liệu tham khảo", which leave a keeper guessing whose claim it is (a Sonnet reader; the Glossary lead, Wed 18 Nov).

What a power cut does is the first shop's alone (facts 53–55), so it sits inside one opening as one sentence, word for word: "Tiệm thứ nhất cũng ghi: khi cúp điện, bơm ngừng vài tiếng là vi khuẩn kỵ khí sinh độc, oxy tụt và vi khuẩn trong lọc yếu đi, nên cá có thể căng thẳng rất nhanh, nhất là khi trời nóng hoặc bể nuôi dày; có điện lại mà đo nước thấy chất độc tăng thì thay một phần nước bằng nước đã khử clo, chứ đừng chỉ bật lọc lên rồi thôi." A full stop ends a credit, so none of it stands after one (a Sonnet reader; the Glossary lead, Wed 18 Nov).

Other names: "dòng chảy mạnh" and "dòng nước" are the site's own link names, on main since the glossary began, and the engine keeps them; any new one only as a fact gives it, with "Water flow" (a Sonnet reader; the Glossary lead, Wed 18 Nov).

A figure keeps its own place: a figure a page measured in one country or climate (a Singapore shop's thaw time, a humid-tropics vitamin loss) is said of that place, or of the climate the page names, never of Vietnam unless a fact names Vietnam (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

No "vì", "nên", "do", "để" or "khiến" joins two facts that no single fact joins: two facts side by side stay two sentences, or are joined with "và" (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A claim only one page makes (one keeper's blog, one shop, a news report) says whose it is ("Một tiệm ghi …", "Một tiệm ở Singapore ghi …", "Một nguồn người nuôi ghi …", "Một bài báo nói …"), with the shop's or keeper's place in those same words when the fact gives it; one such opening can carry several claims of the same page, and a claim two pages make needs none. It is never written as plain fact. A dose or amount several times the entry's main one is left out, or named as the stronger one it is (the chief of staff, Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Every number carries its unit as its fact gives it; a figure whose fact gives no unit (such as a page's "KH 4–5") is left out, or said in the fact's own words ("nước cứng, đệm tốt") (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

An entry names at most three pages this way and doesn't grow to carry more. Past three, it drops the one-page claims a keeper can't act on (why a thing happens, lists of possible causes, background); a one-page claim a keeper acts on (a dose, a time, a step, a warning) waits for a second page from research; what is still over is left out. An entry may come out shorter than its length rather than pad (the chief of staff, Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

The discus line stays inside the first shop's list item, as one sentence, word for word: "Cá lớn hoặc bơi nhanh, như cá đĩa: 8–12 lần thể tích bể mỗi giờ, nhưng nên tránh để dòng mạnh xả thẳng vào cá đĩa." (facts 28, 44: that shop alone); a full stop would leave its second half plain (the second Sonnet reader; the Glossary lead, Wed 18 Nov).

Dead spots: the debris that gathers there is on several pages (facts 5, 18, 21); the tank's corners are one page's (fact 18) and go. Word for word: "Cặn bẩn hay đọng ở đó." (the second Sonnet reader; the Glossary lead, Wed 18 Nov).
The ways to cut the flow are for a betta, as fact 31 says: "Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi: có thể giảm dòng cho cá betta theo các cách sau:" (the second Sonnet reader; the Glossary lead, Wed 18 Nov).

free: Với vây rách, nguồn thứ hai ghi vết rách nhỏ, mép gọn thường tự lành trong một đến hai tuần nếu nước được giữ sạch, không cần thuốc. Nguồn này khuyên không nuôi cá hay rỉa vây chung với cá vây dài và kiểm tra cạnh sắc trên đồ trang trí trước khi thả vào bể. Nguồn này cũng khuyên không chữa vây bằng muối cho cá không vảy.

Một nguồn khác ghi trong bể nuôi chung, vây rách thường là do bị cá khác rỉa, và cá vây dài hay bị nhắm tới. Cây nhựa có cạnh sắc, đá nhám và san hô vỡ cũng có thể làm vướng rách vây. Vây bị rỉa hay vướng rách thì mép khá gọn và phần thịt quanh đó trông vẫn khỏe. Còn thối vây thì mép đổi màu và ngày càng nặng hơn.
Một nguồn ghi vây cụp là khi cá xếp vây ép sát thân thay vì xòe ra. Theo nguồn này, vây cụp là dấu hiệu cá đang căng thẳng hoặc bệnh, bản thân nó không phải một bệnh.
Một tiệm ở Việt Nam ghi cá rồng châu Á dòng kim long có 15–19 tia vây lưng và khoảng 25–27 tia ở vây phía sau. Tiệm này dựa vào số tia để chọn cá.
Vây lưng là vây đơn mọc giữa sống lưng của hầu hết các loài cá. Nó giữ cho cá không bị lật nghiêng khi bơi và giúp cá rẽ gấp.
Nguồn về vây cụp nêu một sai lầm là coi như đã xong trong khi cá vẫn cụp vây. Vây còn cụp nghĩa là nguyên nhân vẫn còn đó.
Cũng theo nguồn này, vây cụp do môi trường thường đỡ trong 24–72 giờ sau khi sửa lại nước.
Ở một số loài, vây lưng có gai cứng và nhọn để tự vệ, và gai của vài loài có nọc độc.

write: Moss plants (the site's moss pages) are plants and are never mixed with algae. Algae is called "rêu" or "rêu hại" only where a page calls it so (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026).

Each kind of algae is named as a Vietnamese shop or the site writes it, with the English only as a source writes it. A kind's cause and fix go only with that kind, as its fact gives them, never carried to another kind (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026).
Each cause only as a fact gives it, with the kind of algae its fact names. A "balance" explanation only if a fact gives one (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026).
Algae eaters by the site's own names, each for the algae its fact names, never as eating every kind (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026).

Algaecides: what they do, and their warning for fish, shrimp and plants, only as a fact gives them. Oxy hòa tan's entry is linked where a fact ties algae dying to oxygen (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026).

A figure keeps its own place: a figure a page measured in one country or climate (a Singapore shop's thaw time, a humid-tropics vitamin loss) is said of that place, or of the climate the page names, never of Vietnam unless a fact names Vietnam (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

No "vì", "nên", "do", "để" or "khiến" joins two facts that no single fact joins: two facts side by side stay two sentences, or are joined with "và" (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A claim only one page makes (one keeper's blog, one shop, a news report) says whose it is ("Một tiệm ghi …", "Một tiệm ở Singapore ghi …", "Một nguồn người nuôi ghi …", "Một bài báo nói …"), with the shop's or keeper's place in those same words when the fact gives it; one such opening can carry several claims of the same page, and a claim two pages make needs none. It is never written as plain fact. A dose or amount several times the entry's main one is left out, or named as the stronger one it is (the chief of staff, Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Every number carries its unit as its fact gives it; a figure whose fact gives no unit (such as a page's "KH 4–5") is left out, or said in the fact's own words ("nước cứng, đệm tốt") (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

An entry names at most three pages this way and doesn't grow to carry more. Past three, it drops the one-page claims a keeper can't act on (why a thing happens, lists of possible causes, background); a one-page claim a keeper acts on (a dose, a time, a step, a warning) waits for a second page from research; what is still over is left out. An entry may come out shorter than its length rather than pad (the chief of staff, Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

When two or more claims in a row are one page's, they go under one opening, as a list or as one sentence with semicolons, never an opening per sentence; a list under an opening counts as credited, each item included (the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term, from Thu 19's first writes).

Two pages of one site are credited apart in neutral words: the first as its facts call it ("Một tiệm ghi:"), the second "Một bài khác ghi:". They are never called another shop and never another page of the same shop, because no fact says whose site a page is. Two different shops keep "Một tiệm ghi:", "Một tiệm khác ghi:", then "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi:" (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A group of fish is named by a name the site has a page for, or by the scientific name its fact writes. Otherwise, where the fact speaks of the whole group, the sentence uses the fact's own word for the group, with no "một số"; where it speaks of some of a group, it says "một số loài" with the fact's widest word. Never "nhiều" or "các loài", which widen the fact (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term, in place of Thu 19's).

A fact's own hedges and amounts stay as it gives them: a hedge is never dropped or added, and an amount is never rounded, widened or narrowed (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Two pages of one site are one source: they count as one toward the three pages an entry names, and a claim only one site's pages give is that site's claim and carries its credit; a claim two sites give stands plain (the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A term's meaning rests on two sites where two define it. Where only one does, it says only what that fact gives and stands without a credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A claim stands plain when two sites carry it: one gives it as broadly as the sentence says it, and another gives the same thing in other words, or for some of the cases it covers. Where a fact limits the claim, the limit is said beside it; if it isn't, the claim takes the credit of the site that gives it broadly. A claim only one site gives takes that site's credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A Vietnamese word that plainly translates another site's word for a thing is the thing's name and needs no credit. A word that is not a plain translation, or a trade name only one shop uses, stays that shop's word, under its credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Each thing is named as its fact names it. A substance, product or tool never takes the name of another, even one keepers use in its place (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A plain sentence says only what two sites give. A part that only one site gives goes in its own sentence under that site's credit, never joined to the two-site part in one sentence (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A word the entry uses for one thing (a name, a shape, a sign) is never used in it for another. Where two things share a fact's word, the second gets a plain word of its own (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).
A name in brackets under a page's credit is that page's own word for the thing, or it isn't there (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A sentence that only sends the reader to the site's own entry or tool is no claim and needs no outside source. It is a pointer and says nothing more: "<what>: xem mục <entry>." or "Kiểm tra <what> bằng <tool> của AquaTome." A sentence that says what a thing is, what it does or which group it is in needs an outside source even when it links the site's page (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Each source's claims are kept together where the order allows. A source named again is "tiệm này", "hội này" or "nguồn người nuôi này" while it is the last of its kind named. Where it comes back after another of its kind, it is "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi:", as Thu 19's line says. If the second hasn't been introduced yet, it is named by what its page gave or is about ("Tiệm kể các loại tảo ở trên", "Nguồn người nuôi viết về Betta tự cắn đuôi"). "kia", "nói ở trên" and "khác ở trên" are not used (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A page's kind as research gives it (a shop, a society, a keeper, a paper, a reference) may open its credit; a kind no research gives is not used (the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Only the sentences listed here as changing change; every other sentence, heading and list stays word for word where the saved entry has it (the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: the Writing Lead's wording revises, applied exactly as it wrote them).

Tiệm thứ hai cũng xếp mấy việc sau vào sai lầm hay gặp: dùng oxy già quá tay, bật đèn suốt ngày đêm, cho ăn quá nhiều và thay 100% nước.
Rêu chùm đen (Black Beard Algae): búi đen, xanh sẫm hoặc đỏ sẫm trên mép lá, lũa và đá, ưa chỗ nước chảy mạnh.
Có thể gỡ bằng tay và bớt châm sắt.
Số ngày tắt đèn thì mỗi nguồn ghi một khác: 5 ngày, 5–7 ngày, hoặc ít nhất một tuần.
Tiệm này cũng xếp mấy việc sau vào sai lầm hay gặp: dùng oxy già quá tay, bật đèn suốt ngày đêm, cho ăn quá nhiều và thay 100% nước.
Kháng sinh erythromycin cũng diệt được nó. Hội này ghi: dùng nửa liều cũng diệt được.

Tảo nâu (diatom): lớp nâu nhớt bám lỏng trên kính, đá và lũa. Silicat và phosphate cao nuôi nó. Tiệm này cũng ghi: ở bể mới thì chờ 4–6 tuần cho nó tự ổn, hoặc chà đi. Hội này cũng ghi: Otocinclus ăn tảo nâu.
Rêu đốm xanh: đốm xanh nhỏ, cứng trên kính, đá, lũa và lá to, cứng. Hội này khuyên châm phosphate lên 0,5–2,0 ppm.
Rêu tóc (Oedogonium): sợi xanh mảnh như tóc trên lá, đá, lũa, nền và kính. Nó mọc khi sắt trên 0,15 ppm. Có thể gỡ tảo ra.
Dư sắt làm nó mọc.

length.why: Choosing, rinsing and laying sand are steps a keeper follows. The chief of staff's rule, 15 Nov 2026: 500 for a term whose facts carry steps a keeper follows or a set of forms, about 400 for any other.

write: How much and how often as each fact gives it, with its unit, saying whose it is when one page gives it. Never one rule for all tanks unless two pages give the same (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026).

The steps in the order the facts give them. Chu trình nitơ's, Nitrat's and Amoniac's entries are linked where a fact ties them (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026).

What tap water holds and how it is treated is said of Vietnam only where a fact names Vietnam. Water conditioner brands only as a fact names them (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026).
The risks of a big change only as facts give them (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026).
Fry tanks: Cá bột's entry is linked, and its figures aren't repeated (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026).

A figure keeps its own place: a figure a page measured in one country or climate (a Singapore shop's thaw time, a humid-tropics vitamin loss) is said of that place, or of the climate the page names, never of Vietnam unless a fact names Vietnam (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

No "vì", "nên", "do", "để" or "khiến" joins two facts that no single fact joins: two facts side by side stay two sentences, or are joined with "và" (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A claim only one page makes (one keeper's blog, one shop, a news report) says whose it is ("Một tiệm ghi …", "Một tiệm ở Singapore ghi …", "Một nguồn người nuôi ghi …", "Một bài báo nói …"), with the shop's or keeper's place in those same words when the fact gives it; one such opening can carry several claims of the same page, and a claim two pages make needs none. It is never written as plain fact. A dose or amount several times the entry's main one is left out, or named as the stronger one it is (the chief of staff, Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Every number carries its unit as its fact gives it; a figure whose fact gives no unit (such as a page's "KH 4–5") is left out, or said in the fact's own words ("nước cứng, đệm tốt") (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

An entry names at most three pages this way and doesn't grow to carry more. Past three, it drops the one-page claims a keeper can't act on (why a thing happens, lists of possible causes, background); a one-page claim a keeper acts on (a dose, a time, a step, a warning) waits for a second page from research; what is still over is left out. An entry may come out shorter than its length rather than pad (the chief of staff, Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

When two or more claims in a row are one page's, they go under one opening, as a list or as one sentence with semicolons, never an opening per sentence; a list under an opening counts as credited, each item included (the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term, from Thu 19's first writes).

Two pages of one site are credited apart in neutral words: the first as its facts call it ("Một tiệm ghi:"), the second "Một bài khác ghi:". They are never called another shop and never another page of the same shop, because no fact says whose site a page is. Two different shops keep "Một tiệm ghi:", "Một tiệm khác ghi:", then "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi:" (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A group of fish is named by a name the site has a page for, or by the scientific name its fact writes. Otherwise, where the fact speaks of the whole group, the sentence uses the fact's own word for the group, with no "một số"; where it speaks of some of a group, it says "một số loài" with the fact's widest word. Never "nhiều" or "các loài", which widen the fact (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term, in place of Thu 19's).

A fact's own hedges and amounts stay as it gives them: a hedge is never dropped or added, and an amount is never rounded, widened or narrowed (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Two pages of one site are one source: they count as one toward the three pages an entry names, and a claim only one site's pages give is that site's claim and carries its credit; a claim two sites give stands plain (the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A term's meaning rests on two sites where two define it. Where only one does, it says only what that fact gives and stands without a credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A claim stands plain when two sites carry it: one gives it as broadly as the sentence says it, and another gives the same thing in other words, or for some of the cases it covers. Where a fact limits the claim, the limit is said beside it; if it isn't, the claim takes the credit of the site that gives it broadly. A claim only one site gives takes that site's credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A Vietnamese word that plainly translates another site's word for a thing is the thing's name and needs no credit. A word that is not a plain translation, or a trade name only one shop uses, stays that shop's word, under its credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Each thing is named as its fact names it. A substance, product or tool never takes the name of another, even one keepers use in its place (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A plain sentence says only what two sites give. A part that only one site gives goes in its own sentence under that site's credit, never joined to the two-site part in one sentence (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A word the entry uses for one thing (a name, a shape, a sign) is never used in it for another. Where two things share a fact's word, the second gets a plain word of its own (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).
A name in brackets under a page's credit is that page's own word for the thing, or it isn't there (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A sentence that only sends the reader to the site's own entry or tool is no claim and needs no outside source. It is a pointer and says nothing more: "<what>: xem mục <entry>." or "Kiểm tra <what> bằng <tool> của AquaTome." A sentence that says what a thing is, what it does or which group it is in needs an outside source even when it links the site's page (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Each source's claims are kept together where the order allows. A source named again is "tiệm này", "hội này" or "nguồn người nuôi này" while it is the last of its kind named. Where it comes back after another of its kind, it is "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi:", as Thu 19's line says. If the second hasn't been introduced yet, it is named by what its page gave or is about ("Tiệm kể các loại tảo ở trên", "Nguồn người nuôi viết về Betta tự cắn đuôi"). "kia", "nói ở trên" and "khác ở trên" are not used (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A page's kind as research gives it (a shop, a society, a keeper, a paper, a reference) may open its credit; a kind no research gives is not used (the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Tap water's chlorine keeps both facts' words: "thường" (fact 43, a Vietnamese shop) and "clo hoặc cloramin" (fact 28), never a plain "Nước máy có clo". Standing, aerating or boiling is said only of chlorine (facts 26 and 36); aging doesn't remove chloramine (fact 27), so no sentence reads as if aerating were enough for chloramine (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026, on the stop's notes).

A heading ends "này". The first sentence under a heading that comes back to a source names it again: "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai", or by what its page gave, where two of its kind have been named. "Hội này", "tiệm này" or "nguồn người nuôi này" stay only where a single source of that kind has been named on the page (the Writing Lead, with the chief of staff's yes, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A medicine named in an entry by its name (erythromycin, muối hồ cá) carries no amount: no dose, no part of a dose ("nửa liều", "gấp đôi"), no length of a course. Straight after the sentence that names it comes one sentence, which says nothing more: where the site has an open guide on that disease, "Liều và cách dùng: xem bài <the guide's title>."; where it has none, the guide is held or gone, or the medicine is used on something that isn't a fish disease (algae, say), "Liều và cách dùng: theo nhãn thuốc." A line that sends the reader to treatment without naming a medicine is a pointer: "Cách chữa <the disease>: xem bài <the guide's title>." Neither ever points to "bài hướng dẫn chữa bệnh", which is no page, nor to the guides list. Until a guide's link is in, its title stands as plain words (the Writing Lead, with the chief of staff's yes and rider, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Tap water, within three named pages: "Nước máy thường có clo hoặc cloramin, đều độc với cá." in place of "Nước máy có clo, độc với cá.", plain and uncredited (facts 28 and 43, two sites; the vet's page stays unnamed). "Sục khí cũng khử được clo." goes; the first Vietnamese shop's own claims take fact 36 in its words: "muốn bỏ clo mà không dùng chất xử lý nước thì sục khí mạnh 1–2 giờ, hoặc để nước ngoài nắng 24 giờ". Nothing says standing, aerating or boiling removes chloramine (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026, on the reader's fact points).

Alkalinity keeps the facts' word, "độ kiềm", wherever the magazine's facts (7 to 11) say it; "KH" is not used for it, and "tức phần KH giữ pH ổn định" is cut (no fact makes that link): "Vi khuẩn nitrat hóa dùng hết cacbonat và bicacbonat, chất đệm giữ pH." in place of "Vi khuẩn nitrat hóa dùng dần cacbonat và bicacbonat, tức phần KH giữ pH ổn định." (fact 7's "use up") (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

A source met again: "Tạp chí này" for "Tạp chí trên" (twice); "Tiệm thứ nhất cũng ghi" where the first shop comes back after the second (its steps; its 100% line is the Writing Lead's sentence below, word for word); "Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi:" where the second comes back after the first (the credit forms line; the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

These are written word for word, each in place of the draft's sentence named (the facts' own words; the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026): "Đo amoniac, nitrit và nitrat sau khi châm nước." in place of "Châm nước mới nhẹ tay để không khuấy nền, châm xong thì đo amoniac, nitrit và nitrat." (slow refilling is said once, in the first shop's step 5; fact 24) / "Dấu hiệu cá căng thẳng sau khi chuyển bể hay thay nước gồm đổi màu, ít hoạt động, bỏ ăn và đỏ mắt." (fact 42's "include"; no "có thể"; "low activity").

These are written word for word, each in place of the saved sentence, meaning or step named (the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026 evening batch, with the chief of staff's rulings): "Thay nước là hút bớt một phần nước cũ trong bể cùng chất bẩn dưới nền, rồi châm nước mới vào; nước máy thì phải khử clo trước." in place of "Thay nước là hút bớt một phần nước cũ trong bể cùng chất bẩn dưới nền, rồi châm nước mới đã khử clo vào." / "Cá có thể chết không lâu sau lần thay đó." in place of "Cá có thể chết ngay sau lần thay đó." / "Tạp chí này: muốn giữ chất dinh dưỡng và độ kiềm trong tầm kiểm soát thì lúc đầu thay ít nhất 20% nước, mỗi tháng một lần." in place of "Tạp chí trên: muốn giữ chất dinh dưỡng và KH trong tầm thì lúc đầu thay ít nhất 20% nước, mỗi tháng một lần." / "Ba nguồn ghi ba mức thay khác nhau:" in place of "Mỗi nguồn ghi một mức thay khác nhau:" / "Tắt máy bơm, máy sưởi và đèn." in place of "Tắt máy bơm, sưởi và đèn." / "Tiệm thứ nhất ghi rằng thay 100% nước sẽ làm mất vi khuẩn có lợi đã ổn định trong bể và làm cá sốc, có thể khiến cá lờ đờ, thậm chí chết hàng loạt." in place of "Tiệm thứ nhất ghi rằng thay 100% nước sẽ phá đàn vi khuẩn đã ổn định và làm cá sốc, có thể khiến cá lờ đờ, thậm chí chết hàng loạt." / "Châm nước mới từ từ, không dội thẳng vào cá, và chỉnh dần nhiệt độ nước mới cho bằng nhiệt độ bể. Nhiệt độ bể không nên đổi quá 0,5 °C mỗi giờ." in place of "Châm nước mới từ từ, không dội thẳng vào cá, và đưa nhiệt độ về dần. Nhiệt độ bể không nên đổi quá 0,5 °C mỗi giờ."

The heading "Trong bể của bạn" becomes "Nước dùng để thay" (the Writing Lead, by the heading rule): the section is tap water's chlorine, what the water brings back, RO and distilled water, and coral for soft tap water. Its sentences stay under it as they are, but for those named in these lines.
Each sentence and item not named in these lines stays word for word where the saved entry has it (the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: revises change only what their notes name).

This sentence is cut, and nothing takes its place: "Tiệm này còn ghi rằng muốn bỏ clo mà không dùng chất xử lý nước thì sục khí mạnh 1–2 giờ, hoặc để nước ngoài nắng 24 giờ." The shops' times are several-fold apart, and standing water does not take chloramine out (the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026, as with Tảo's peroxide). The meaning already says tap water must be dechlorinated, and the second shop's thiosulfate line stays.
free: Nước máy có clo, độc với cá.
Sục khí cũng khử được clo.
Vi khuẩn nitrat hóa dùng dần cacbonat và bicacbonat, tức phần KH giữ pH ổn định.
Châm nước mới nhẹ tay để không khuấy nền, châm xong thì đo amoniac, nitrit và nitrat.
Cá căng thẳng sau khi chuyển bể hay thay nước có thể có các dấu hiệu như đổi màu, ít bơi, bỏ ăn, đỏ mắt.
Thay nước là hút bớt một phần nước cũ trong bể cùng chất bẩn dưới nền, rồi châm nước mới đã khử clo vào.
Cá có thể chết ngay sau lần thay đó.
Tạp chí trên: muốn giữ chất dinh dưỡng và KH trong tầm thì lúc đầu thay ít nhất 20% nước, mỗi tháng một lần.
Mỗi nguồn ghi một mức thay khác nhau:
Tắt máy bơm, sưởi và đèn.
Tiệm thứ nhất ghi rằng thay 100% nước sẽ phá đàn vi khuẩn đã ổn định và làm cá sốc, có thể khiến cá lờ đờ, thậm chí chết hàng loạt.
Châm nước mới từ từ, không dội thẳng vào cá, và đưa nhiệt độ về dần. Nhiệt độ bể không nên đổi quá 0,5 °C mỗi giờ.
Trong bể của bạn
Tiệm này còn ghi rằng muốn bỏ clo mà không dùng chất xử lý nước thì sục khí mạnh 1–2 giờ, hoặc để nước ngoài nắng 24 giờ.
