free: Một nguồn thú y đưa quy tắc ước chừng khoảng 2,5 cm cá trưởng thành cho mỗi 3,8 lít nước, và lấy ví dụ bể 38 lít nuôi được hai đàn, mỗi đàn 5 con cá dưới 2,5 cm.
Về số cá một bể chứa được, các nguồn không thống nhất.
Nguồn thú y khuyên đợt đầu chọn loài khỏe và không giành chỗ, rồi chia cá theo tầng mặt, tầng giữa và tầng đáy cho cân.
Nguồn thú y ghi chạy 1–2 tuần, đo nước mỗi ngày, và bỏ bước này thì có nguy cơ gặp hội chứng bể mới.
Bài viết ghi khoảng 2–6 tuần, dùng vi sinh mồi hoặc một chút thức ăn làm nguồn amoniac.
Thả cá từng đợt, mỗi đợt cách nhau vài tuần.
Thả cá đáy và cá đàn trước, cá betta (cá xiêm) sau cùng.
Với cá betta (cá xiêm), nên chọn con mái hoặc dòng plakat, vì con trống hay giành chỗ là mối lo chính.
Thả quá đông.
Nguồn thú y ghi chất thải sẽ tích lại, nước xấu đi và cá đánh nhau.
Thả quá đông làm bể tốn công chăm hơn và chịu kém khi oxy tụt.
Thả cá mới thẳng vào bể đang chạy mà không cách ly trong bể riêng trước.
Thả cá chênh cỡ nhiều.
Con nào nhỏ đủ lọt miệng con khác thì có nguy cơ bị ăn.
Hay gặp trong bể chung có Corydoras, cá neon xanh, cá ember tetra, cá mún, cá bảy màu, cá molly, cá tam giác và cá anh đào.
Nó có thể ăn tép red cherry con.
Ghép cá vây dài như cá bảy màu kiểu (fancy guppy) với cá hay rỉa vây như tiger barb.
Một bài viết bác quy tắc "1 cm cá cho 1 lít" và tính số cá theo cỡ cá lúc lớn, nhu cầu sống đàn, tính lãnh thổ, lượng chất thải và diện tích mặt nước.
Cho bể chạy lọc qua chu trình nitơ rồi mới thả cá.
Cho ăn quá tay làm tăng amoniac và nitrat.
Cách ly cá mới trong bể riêng trước khi thả vào bể đã nuôi sẵn.
Tạp chí cá cảnh này ghi: cách ly cá mới trong bể riêng trước khi thả vào bể đã nuôi sẵn.
Cho cá mới quen dần với nhiệt độ và nước bể.

length.why: Choosing and adding fish are steps a keeper follows. The chief of staff's rule, 15 Nov 2026: 500 for a term whose facts carry steps a keeper follows or a set of forms, about 400 for any other.

write: What counts as live food only as the facts name it. Each food by the name Vietnamese shops or the site write it, the English only as a source writes it (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

A food that has a term of its own on the site (Artemia, Bo bo, Trùng huyết, Trùng chỉ, Trùng cỏ) is linked. It is said in a line, and none of its entry's steps or figures is repeated (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

Each food keeps its own facts: what one food does or carries is never said of another, or of all live food (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

Disease or parasites live food brings in, and how a source says to lower that risk, only as a fact gives it, with that fact's source (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
Wild-caught and raised food only as facts tell them apart (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
Which fish it is fed to, by the site's own names, as each fact gives them (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
Thức ăn đông lạnh's and Thức ăn khô's entries are linked for the other forms, their steps not repeated (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
The entry writes "thức ăn sống". "mồi sống" and "thức ăn tươi sống" are other names only as a page uses them (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

A figure keeps its own place: a figure a page measured in one country or climate (a Singapore shop's thaw time, a humid-tropics vitamin loss) is said of that place, or of the climate the page names, never of Vietnam unless a fact names Vietnam (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

No "vì", "nên", "do", "để" or "khiến" joins two facts that no single fact joins: two facts side by side stay two sentences, or are joined with "và" (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A claim only one page makes (one keeper's blog, one shop, a news report) says whose it is ("Một tiệm ghi …", "Một tiệm ở Singapore ghi …", "Một nguồn người nuôi ghi …", "Một bài báo nói …"), with the shop's or keeper's place in those same words when the fact gives it; one such opening can carry several claims of the same page, and a claim two pages make needs none. It is never written as plain fact. A dose or amount several times the entry's main one is left out, or named as the stronger one it is (the chief of staff, Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Every number carries its unit as its fact gives it; a figure whose fact gives no unit (such as a page's "KH 4–5") is left out, or said in the fact's own words ("nước cứng, đệm tốt") (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

An entry names at most three pages this way and doesn't grow to carry more. Past three, it drops the one-page claims a keeper can't act on (why a thing happens, lists of possible causes, background); a one-page claim a keeper acts on (a dose, a time, a step, a warning) waits for a second page from research; what is still over is left out. An entry may come out shorter than its length rather than pad (the chief of staff, Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

When two or more claims in a row are one page's, they go under one opening, as a list or as one sentence with semicolons, never an opening per sentence; a list under an opening counts as credited, each item included (the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term, from Thu 19's first writes).

Two pages of one site are credited apart in neutral words: the first as its facts call it ("Một tiệm ghi:"), the second "Một bài khác ghi:". They are never called another shop and never another page of the same shop, because no fact says whose site a page is. Two different shops keep "Một tiệm ghi:", "Một tiệm khác ghi:", then "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi:" (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A group of fish is named by a name the site has a page for, or by the scientific name its fact writes. Otherwise, where the fact speaks of the whole group, the sentence uses the fact's own word for the group, with no "một số"; where it speaks of some of a group, it says "một số loài" with the fact's widest word. Never "nhiều" or "các loài", which widen the fact (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term, in place of Thu 19's).

A fact's own hedges and amounts stay as it gives them: a hedge is never dropped or added, and an amount is never rounded, widened or narrowed (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Two pages of one site are one source: they count as one toward the three pages an entry names, and a claim only one site's pages give is that site's claim and carries its credit; a claim two sites give stands plain (the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A term's meaning rests on two sites where two define it. Where only one does, it says only what that fact gives and stands without a credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A claim stands plain when two sites carry it: one gives it as broadly as the sentence says it, and another gives the same thing in other words, or for some of the cases it covers. Where a fact limits the claim, the limit is said beside it; if it isn't, the claim takes the credit of the site that gives it broadly. A claim only one site gives takes that site's credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A Vietnamese word that plainly translates another site's word for a thing is the thing's name and needs no credit. A word that is not a plain translation, or a trade name only one shop uses, stays that shop's word, under its credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Each thing is named as its fact names it. A substance, product or tool never takes the name of another, even one keepers use in its place (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A plain sentence says only what two sites give. A part that only one site gives goes in its own sentence under that site's credit, never joined to the two-site part in one sentence (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A word the entry uses for one thing (a name, a shape, a sign) is never used in it for another. Where two things share a fact's word, the second gets a plain word of its own (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).
A name in brackets under a page's credit is that page's own word for the thing, or it isn't there (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A sentence that only sends the reader to the site's own entry or tool is no claim and needs no outside source. It is a pointer and says nothing more: "<what>: xem mục <entry>." or "Kiểm tra <what> bằng <tool> của AquaTome." A sentence that says what a thing is, what it does or which group it is in needs an outside source even when it links the site's page (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Each source's claims are kept together where the order allows. A source named again is "tiệm này", "hội này" or "nguồn người nuôi này" while it is the last of its kind named. Where it comes back after another of its kind, it is "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi:", as Thu 19's line says. If the second hasn't been introduced yet, it is named by what its page gave or is about ("Tiệm kể các loại tảo ở trên", "Nguồn người nuôi viết về Betta tự cắn đuôi"). "kia", "nói ở trên" and "khác ở trên" are not used (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A page's kind as research gives it (a shop, a society, a keeper, a paper, a reference) may open its credit; a kind no research gives is not used (the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A heading ends "này". The first sentence under a heading that comes back to a source names it again: "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai", or by what its page gave, where two of its kind have been named. "Hội này", "tiệm này" or "nguồn người nuôi này" stay only where a single source of that kind has been named on the page (the Writing Lead, with the chief of staff's yes, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A medicine named in an entry by its name (erythromycin, muối hồ cá) carries no amount: no dose, no part of a dose ("nửa liều", "gấp đôi"), no length of a course. Straight after the sentence that names it comes one sentence, which says nothing more: where the site has an open guide on that disease, "Liều và cách dùng: xem bài <the guide's title>."; where it has none, the guide is held or gone, or the medicine is used on something that isn't a fish disease (algae, say), "Liều và cách dùng: theo nhãn thuốc." A line that sends the reader to treatment without naming a medicine is a pointer: "Cách chữa <the disease>: xem bài <the guide's title>." Neither ever points to "bài hướng dẫn chữa bệnh", which is no page, nor to the guides list. Until a guide's link is in, its title stands as plain words (the Writing Lead, with the chief of staff's yes and rider, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

The Tubifex block is cut, its opening ("Một tài liệu tham khảo ghi về giun Tubifex:") and its three items: Tubifex is Trùng chỉ's (that entry's Latin name), so by this term's line it is said in one line and linked, as "Trùng chỉ: xem mục Trùng chỉ." already does (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026, on the first reader's fact point and the rules reader's stop).
"Cho cá bột ăn bo bo đã chết hoặc bốc mùi có thể làm cá bệnh." is cut: it is Bo bo's entry's, and Bo bo is said in one line (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026, on the rules reader's stop).

The meaning says only what fact 3 gives (one site defines live food, so it stands uncredited): no list of foods, which no fact gives, and never "mồi" for live food, since the entry uses "cá mồi" for feeder fish (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026, on the first reader's fact point).

These are written word for word, each in place of the draft's sentence named: "Cá mồi mua ở tiệm dễ đem bệnh vào bể hơn, mà phần lớn người nuôi không cách ly chúng." (fact 11's "most keepers", in place of "thường") / "Blackworm không rửa mỗi ngày thì nhanh làm bẩn nước. Cách giữ là để trong hộp nông, sâu không quá 1,3 cm, ngập nước lạnh đã khử clo, rồi cất tủ lạnh." (fact 54's depth is the container's, not the water's) / "Cho ăn mãi một loại thức ăn thì cá có thể thiếu chất." (fact 5's "can", in place of "dễ") / "Ương cá bột chỉ bằng thức ăn sống là sai. Về sau nên tập cho cá ăn thêm thức ăn khô để chúng quen ăn nhiều loại." (fact 7's "should", in place of "phải") (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026, on the first reader's fact points).

"Vinegar eel, micro worm, grindal worm và white worm đều tự nuôi ở nhà được." is cut: no fact says any of them is raised at home, and none gives grindal or white worms' culture. The substrate sentence after it stays (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026, on the first reader's fact point).

Fact 12 names goldfish and minnows sold as feeders: both are named, never goldfish alone (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026, on the first reader's fact point; the word for minnow is the Writing Lead's).

These are written word for word, each in place of the draft's meaning or sentence named (the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026 evening batch, with the chief of staff's rulings): "Thức ăn sống là thức ăn còn sống, còn cử động, nên làm cá muốn ăn. Nó còn kích thích cá cả về thể chất lẫn tinh thần, và là cách nhanh để vỗ cá cho đẻ." in place of "Thức ăn sống là mồi còn sống cho cá ăn, như ấu trùng artemia, bo bo hay trùng chỉ. Mồi cựa quậy làm cá chịu ăn và cho cá vận động cả thân lẫn đầu óc. Đây cũng là cách nhanh để vỗ cá trước khi cho đẻ." / "Cá vàng và cá minnow bán làm cá mồi chứa nhiều thiaminase." in place of "Cá vàng bán làm cá mồi chứa nhiều thiaminase." / "Nhiều người nhân giống cá coi blackworm là cách tốt nhất để vỗ Corydoras." in place of "Nhiều người ép đẻ coi đây là cách tốt nhất để vỗ Corydoras." / "Không vớt hằng ngày thì lăng quăng sẽ thành muỗi." in place of "Không vớt hằng ngày thì lăng quăng sẽ nở thành muỗi." / "Nên cho cá ăn xen kẽ nhiều loại thức ăn." in place of "Đổi nhiều loại cho cá ăn thì hơn.". "Nên cho cá ăn xen kẽ nhiều loại thức ăn." stands plain (two sites).

The six pointers ("Thức ăn đông lạnh: xem mục Thức ăn đông lạnh.", "Thức ăn khô: xem mục Thức ăn khô.", "Artemia: xem mục Artemia.", "Bo bo: xem mục Bo bo.", "Trùng chỉ: xem mục Trùng chỉ.", "Trùng cỏ: xem mục Trùng cỏ.") go together, each as it is, under one heading, "Xem thêm", at the entry's end. The heading "Trong bể của bạn" goes, as it held only two of them. "Các loại thức ăn sống" stays, over the shop's list (the Writing Lead, by the heading rule).
Each sentence and item not named in these lines stays word for word where the draft has it.

The mosquito-larvae item is cut, both its sentences ("Muốn có lăng quăng thì đặt một xô 19 lít nước đã khử clo cho muỗi đẻ, rồi vớt bằng vợt mịn mỗi ngày." and "Không vớt hằng ngày thì lăng quăng sẽ thành muỗi."), and lăng quăng is not written in this entry: setting out standing water for mosquitoes to breed is no advice for Vietnam, where the health service campaigns against it because of dengue, and the source's own caution (scoop daily) doesn't cover it (the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: the owner's row on advice that isn't for Vietnam).

One sentence goes back, in fact 10's own plain words, as the first item under "Sai lầm hay gặp": live food that is not washed well can carry parasites. It takes its site's credit, in the same sentence ("Một … ghi rằng …"), named by its kind as the sources list gives it: only source 9 gives parasites (facts 10 and 23), while facts 31 and 24 give bacteria and disease, not parasites, so it is never plain. Never said of one food alone, since each of those is its own term's. Nothing else is added (the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: the caution main's meaning has today, by the by-day rule, for the Writing Lead's yes after).

The metric figures stay as written, and no note on their units is acted on: "sâu không quá 1,3 cm" and "82–93 °C" are the pages' 0.5 inch and 180–200 °F, as the site writes metric (the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: "0.5 inch is 1,3 cm; 180 to 200°F is 82 to 93 °C").
Every other sentence stays word for word where the saved entry has it (the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: revises change only what their notes name).
free: Một tài liệu tham khảo ghi về giun Tubifex:
Giun rất béo và thiếu một số axit amin thiết yếu. Cá ăn chủ yếu loại này có thể kém khỏe, kém màu.
Giun vớt từ cống, từ nguồn nước ngoài trời hay từ trại nuôi có thể mang nhiều bệnh, nhưng tài liệu này chưa dẫn nguồn cho ý đó.
Giữ giun dưới vòi nước chảy mạnh tới khi chúng thải hết thức ăn trong ruột thì giảm được phần nào nguy cơ này.
Cho cá bột ăn bo bo đã chết hoặc bốc mùi có thể làm cá bệnh.
Vinegar eel, micro worm, grindal worm và white worm đều tự nuôi ở nhà được.
Cá mồi mua ở tiệm dễ đem bệnh vào bể hơn, mà người nuôi thường không cách ly chúng.

free: Ăn tạp là kiểu ăn của những loài cá cần cả thức ăn động vật lẫn thực vật.

Rau cho cá ăn có thể là rau củ luộc, như dưa leo.
Cá tầng đáy cần thức ăn chìm nhanh, còn cá ăn trên mặt nước cần thức ăn nổi.

length.why: A way of feeding, with no steps of its own. The chief of staff's rule, 15 Nov 2026: 500 for a term whose facts carry steps a keeper follows or a set of forms, about 400 for any other.

write: What it is only as the facts give it. When it is stronger or weaker only as a fact gives it (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
Which fish, by the site's own names, each as its fact gives it (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

What a keeper does about it only as facts give it, in their order, every size with its unit and saying whose it is when one page gives it (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
Signs of a fight over ground only as facts give them, as signs to watch, never as a diagnosis (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
"lãnh thổ" is the term's link phrase (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
The name stays "Tính lãnh thổ" for the trait. What a fish does is "giữ lãnh thổ"; "bảo vệ lãnh thổ" only as a page writes it (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
Bể cộng đồng's and Cá đàn's entries are linked where a fact ties them (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

A figure keeps its own place: a figure a page measured in one country or climate (a Singapore shop's thaw time, a humid-tropics vitamin loss) is said of that place, or of the climate the page names, never of Vietnam unless a fact names Vietnam (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

No "vì", "nên", "do", "để" or "khiến" joins two facts that no single fact joins: two facts side by side stay two sentences, or are joined with "và" (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A claim only one page makes (one keeper's blog, one shop, a news report) says whose it is ("Một tiệm ghi …", "Một tiệm ở Singapore ghi …", "Một nguồn người nuôi ghi …", "Một bài báo nói …"), with the shop's or keeper's place in those same words when the fact gives it; one such opening can carry several claims of the same page, and a claim two pages make needs none. It is never written as plain fact. A dose or amount several times the entry's main one is left out, or named as the stronger one it is (the chief of staff, Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Every number carries its unit as its fact gives it; a figure whose fact gives no unit (such as a page's "KH 4–5") is left out, or said in the fact's own words ("nước cứng, đệm tốt") (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

An entry names at most three pages this way and doesn't grow to carry more. Past three, it drops the one-page claims a keeper can't act on (why a thing happens, lists of possible causes, background); a one-page claim a keeper acts on (a dose, a time, a step, a warning) waits for a second page from research; what is still over is left out. An entry may come out shorter than its length rather than pad (the chief of staff, Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

When two or more claims in a row are one page's, they go under one opening, as a list or as one sentence with semicolons, never an opening per sentence; a list under an opening counts as credited, each item included (the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term, from Thu 19's first writes).

Two pages of one site are credited apart in neutral words: the first as its facts call it ("Một tiệm ghi:"), the second "Một bài khác ghi:". They are never called another shop and never another page of the same shop, because no fact says whose site a page is. Two different shops keep "Một tiệm ghi:", "Một tiệm khác ghi:", then "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi:" (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A group of fish is named by a name the site has a page for, or by the scientific name its fact writes. Otherwise, where the fact speaks of the whole group, the sentence uses the fact's own word for the group, with no "một số"; where it speaks of some of a group, it says "một số loài" with the fact's widest word. Never "nhiều" or "các loài", which widen the fact (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term, in place of Thu 19's).

A fact's own hedges and amounts stay as it gives them: a hedge is never dropped or added, and an amount is never rounded, widened or narrowed (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Two pages of one site are one source: they count as one toward the three pages an entry names, and a claim only one site's pages give is that site's claim and carries its credit; a claim two sites give stands plain (the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A term's meaning rests on two sites where two define it. Where only one does, it says only what that fact gives and stands without a credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A claim stands plain when two sites carry it: one gives it as broadly as the sentence says it, and another gives the same thing in other words, or for some of the cases it covers. Where a fact limits the claim, the limit is said beside it; if it isn't, the claim takes the credit of the site that gives it broadly. A claim only one site gives takes that site's credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A Vietnamese word that plainly translates another site's word for a thing is the thing's name and needs no credit. A word that is not a plain translation, or a trade name only one shop uses, stays that shop's word, under its credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Each thing is named as its fact names it. A substance, product or tool never takes the name of another, even one keepers use in its place (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A plain sentence says only what two sites give. A part that only one site gives goes in its own sentence under that site's credit, never joined to the two-site part in one sentence (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A word the entry uses for one thing (a name, a shape, a sign) is never used in it for another. Where two things share a fact's word, the second gets a plain word of its own (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).
A name in brackets under a page's credit is that page's own word for the thing, or it isn't there (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A sentence that only sends the reader to the site's own entry or tool is no claim and needs no outside source. It is a pointer and says nothing more: "<what>: xem mục <entry>." or "Kiểm tra <what> bằng <tool> của AquaTome." A sentence that says what a thing is, what it does or which group it is in needs an outside source even when it links the site's page (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Each source's claims are kept together where the order allows. A source named again is "tiệm này", "hội này" or "nguồn người nuôi này" while it is the last of its kind named. Where it comes back after another of its kind, it is "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi:", as Thu 19's line says. If the second hasn't been introduced yet, it is named by what its page gave or is about ("Tiệm kể các loại tảo ở trên", "Nguồn người nuôi viết về Betta tự cắn đuôi"). "kia", "nói ở trên" and "khác ở trên" are not used (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A page's kind as research gives it (a shop, a society, a keeper, a paper, a reference) may open its credit; a kind no research gives is not used (the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A heading ends "này". The first sentence under a heading that comes back to a source names it again: "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai", or by what its page gave, where two of its kind have been named. "Hội này", "tiệm này" or "nguồn người nuôi này" stay only where a single source of that kind has been named on the page (the Writing Lead, with the chief of staff's yes, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A medicine named in an entry by its name (erythromycin, muối hồ cá) carries no amount: no dose, no part of a dose ("nửa liều", "gấp đôi"), no length of a course. Straight after the sentence that names it comes one sentence, which says nothing more: where the site has an open guide on that disease, "Liều và cách dùng: xem bài <the guide's title>."; where it has none, the guide is held or gone, or the medicine is used on something that isn't a fish disease (algae, say), "Liều và cách dùng: theo nhãn thuốc." A line that sends the reader to treatment without naming a medicine is a pointer: "Cách chữa <the disease>: xem bài <the guide's title>." Neither ever points to "bài hướng dẫn chữa bệnh", which is no page, nor to the guides list. Until a guide's link is in, its title stands as plain words (the Writing Lead, with the chief of staff's yes and rider, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

The meaning says only what fact 0 gives (one site defines it, so it stands uncredited): fish defend places they use to rest, hide or breed. No "thói quen", no chasing (no fact gives either), and places, not one place. "Người nuôi cần biết vì vết thương do bị đánh dễ nhiễm trùng." is cut: no fact says keepers need to know it, and its "vì" joins what no fact joins. The meaning's words are the Writing Lead's where tonight's answers give them (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026, on the first reader's fact points).

"Cá có tính lãnh thổ giữ lãnh thổ của nó và đuổi cá khác ra khỏi đó." and "Dùng đá, cây và lũa để chia bể thành nhiều khu và làm chỗ trốn." are cut: the first repeats the meaning and no fact gives chasing; the second joins one unnamed page's "separate territories" (fact 38) to the hiding places the shop's steps and the study already give (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

These are written word for word, each in place of the draft's sentence or item named (the facts' own words; the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026, on the first reader's fact points): "cá betta có thể đánh cả cá không phải betta mà có màu đỏ, như cá hồng nhung" (fact 4; "(cá xiêm)" cut, since the shop writes Betta splendens; and its "may attack non-betta fish that are red" is no condition) / "dấu hiệu cá đánh nhau gồm cá bỗng trốn, vây bị xẻ, trầy xước và mất vảy" as the shop's list's last item, in place of the plain "Những dấu hiệu nên để ý gồm cá bỗng trốn biệt, rách vây, tróc vảy hay trầy xước." (fact 11 is the shop's alone) / "khi thả thêm đá, cây, vật cản khác và chỗ trốn, cá bớt thời gian dọa nhau và đánh nhau, nhưng cá chỉ bớt hung ở môi trường đủ lớn và phức tạp" (facts 37 and 18: the hiding places are their own thing, and fact 18's "only") / "Nếu cá đánh nhau mãi, bày lại đồ trang trí để cá phải giữ lãnh thổ mới, và thêm chỗ trốn cùng vật che tầm nhìn." (fact 21's new territories) / "Con bắt nạt vẫn thấy những con khác nhưng không đánh được con nào." Cá có tính lãnh thổ giữ lãnh thổ của nó và đuổi cá khác ra khỏi đó.
Dùng đá, cây và lũa để chia bể thành nhiều khu và làm chỗ trốn.
Những dấu hiệu nên để ý gồm cá bỗng trốn biệt, rách vây, tróc vảy hay trầy xước.
Con bắt nạt vẫn thấy đàn nhưng không đánh được con nào.
Một nguồn người nuôi ghi:
Tính lãnh thổ là thói quen của cá khi nó giữ một chỗ trong bể để nghỉ, trốn hay đẻ, và đuổi cá khác khỏi chỗ đó. Người nuôi cần biết vì vết thương do bị đánh dễ nhiễm trùng.
cá càng lớn thì vùng nó giữ càng rộng, nên cần tính trước chỗ cho nó
cá hung nhất với con cùng loài và cùng giới
cá trong bể tự chia thứ bậc, và thứ bậc này có thể đổi khi cá lớn lên
Cách chắc ăn duy nhất nguồn này tìm được là chuyển một con hay gây sự sang bể khác.

Tiệm này cũng ghi: bày lại bể khi thả cá mới để cá mới không phải bắt đầu mà chưa có lãnh thổ; cá tứ vân là cá đàn không giữ lãnh thổ, và nuôi từ 6 con trở lên thì chúng ít có khả năng rỉa vây cá khác hơn.
Tiệm này ghi rằng cứ vớt cá ra rồi thả vào nhiều lần thì ít khi giải quyết được chuyện đánh nhau lâu dài.

length.why: What a keeper does about it (space, layout, the order fish go in) is steps a keeper follows. The chief of staff's rule, 15 Nov 2026: 500 for a term whose facts carry steps a keeper follows or a set of forms, about 400 for any other.

write: Lá bàng's entry is linked. Lá khô says only what is leaf litter's own and repeats none of Lá bàng's lines (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

Each leaf by the name Vietnamese shops or the site write it, with its own facts. What one leaf does is never said of another, or of all leaves (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

What leaves do to the water only as facts give it. Tanin's and pH's entries are linked where a fact ties them (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
Which fish live among leaves, by the site's own names, as each fact gives them (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
Where leaves come from, and what a source says to check before use, only as facts give it (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
"lớp lá khô" and "lá mục" are the term's link phrases, never printed as other names (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
The entry comes in no kinds: no leaf gets an item of its own with a photo (the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026; Curation's question on Sat 21).

A figure keeps its own place: a figure a page measured in one country or climate (a Singapore shop's thaw time, a humid-tropics vitamin loss) is said of that place, or of the climate the page names, never of Vietnam unless a fact names Vietnam (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

No "vì", "nên", "do", "để" or "khiến" joins two facts that no single fact joins: two facts side by side stay two sentences, or are joined with "và" (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A claim only one page makes (one keeper's blog, one shop, a news report) says whose it is ("Một tiệm ghi …", "Một tiệm ở Singapore ghi …", "Một nguồn người nuôi ghi …", "Một bài báo nói …"), with the shop's or keeper's place in those same words when the fact gives it; one such opening can carry several claims of the same page, and a claim two pages make needs none. It is never written as plain fact. A dose or amount several times the entry's main one is left out, or named as the stronger one it is (the chief of staff, Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Every number carries its unit as its fact gives it; a figure whose fact gives no unit (such as a page's "KH 4–5") is left out, or said in the fact's own words ("nước cứng, đệm tốt") (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

An entry names at most three pages this way and doesn't grow to carry more. Past three, it drops the one-page claims a keeper can't act on (why a thing happens, lists of possible causes, background); a one-page claim a keeper acts on (a dose, a time, a step, a warning) waits for a second page from research; what is still over is left out. An entry may come out shorter than its length rather than pad (the chief of staff, Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

When two or more claims in a row are one page's, they go under one opening, as a list or as one sentence with semicolons, never an opening per sentence; a list under an opening counts as credited, each item included (the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term, from Thu 19's first writes).

Two pages of one site are credited apart in neutral words: the first as its facts call it ("Một tiệm ghi:"), the second "Một bài khác ghi:". They are never called another shop and never another page of the same shop, because no fact says whose site a page is. Two different shops keep "Một tiệm ghi:", "Một tiệm khác ghi:", then "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi:" (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A group of fish is named by a name the site has a page for, or by the scientific name its fact writes. Otherwise, where the fact speaks of the whole group, the sentence uses the fact's own word for the group, with no "một số"; where it speaks of some of a group, it says "một số loài" with the fact's widest word. Never "nhiều" or "các loài", which widen the fact (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term, in place of Thu 19's).

A fact's own hedges and amounts stay as it gives them: a hedge is never dropped or added, and an amount is never rounded, widened or narrowed (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Two pages of one site are one source: they count as one toward the three pages an entry names, and a claim only one site's pages give is that site's claim and carries its credit; a claim two sites give stands plain (the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A term's meaning rests on two sites where two define it. Where only one does, it says only what that fact gives and stands without a credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A claim stands plain when two sites carry it: one gives it as broadly as the sentence says it, and another gives the same thing in other words, or for some of the cases it covers. Where a fact limits the claim, the limit is said beside it; if it isn't, the claim takes the credit of the site that gives it broadly. A claim only one site gives takes that site's credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A Vietnamese word that plainly translates another site's word for a thing is the thing's name and needs no credit. A word that is not a plain translation, or a trade name only one shop uses, stays that shop's word, under its credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Each thing is named as its fact names it. A substance, product or tool never takes the name of another, even one keepers use in its place (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A plain sentence says only what two sites give. A part that only one site gives goes in its own sentence under that site's credit, never joined to the two-site part in one sentence (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A word the entry uses for one thing (a name, a shape, a sign) is never used in it for another. Where two things share a fact's word, the second gets a plain word of its own (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).
A name in brackets under a page's credit is that page's own word for the thing, or it isn't there (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A sentence that only sends the reader to the site's own entry or tool is no claim and needs no outside source. It is a pointer and says nothing more: "<what>: xem mục <entry>." or "Kiểm tra <what> bằng <tool> của AquaTome." A sentence that says what a thing is, what it does or which group it is in needs an outside source even when it links the site's page (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Each source's claims are kept together where the order allows. A source named again is "tiệm này", "hội này" or "nguồn người nuôi này" while it is the last of its kind named. Where it comes back after another of its kind, it is "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi:", as Thu 19's line says. If the second hasn't been introduced yet, it is named by what its page gave or is about ("Tiệm kể các loại tảo ở trên", "Nguồn người nuôi viết về Betta tự cắn đuôi"). "kia", "nói ở trên" and "khác ở trên" are not used (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A page's kind as research gives it (a shop, a society, a keeper, a paper, a reference) may open its credit; a kind no research gives is not used (the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A heading ends "này". The first sentence under a heading that comes back to a source names it again: "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai", or by what its page gave, where two of its kind have been named. "Hội này", "tiệm này" or "nguồn người nuôi này" stay only where a single source of that kind has been named on the page (the Writing Lead, with the chief of staff's yes, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A medicine named in an entry by its name (erythromycin, muối hồ cá) carries no amount: no dose, no part of a dose ("nửa liều", "gấp đôi"), no length of a course. Straight after the sentence that names it comes one sentence, which says nothing more: where the site has an open guide on that disease, "Liều và cách dùng: xem bài <the guide's title>."; where it has none, the guide is held or gone, or the medicine is used on something that isn't a fish disease (algae, say), "Liều và cách dùng: theo nhãn thuốc." A line that sends the reader to treatment without naming a medicine is a pointer: "Cách chữa <the disease>: xem bài <the guide's title>." Neither ever points to "bài hướng dẫn chữa bệnh", which is no page, nor to the guides list. Until a guide's link is in, its title stands as plain words (the Writing Lead, with the chief of staff's yes and rider, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

The meaning is fact 3 alone (one site defines leaf litter, so it says only what that fact gives, uncredited): "Khi mục, lá nhả tanin làm pH hạ, và lớp lá là chỗ cá bột kiếm ăn." is cut; the body says each once (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026, on the first reader's fact points).

"Khi mục dần, lá khô nhả tanin và pH trong bể hạ xuống." stands plain (fact 4, two sites), and fact 8's limit goes right after it, under the magazine's credit, in the fact's words: the leaves' pH effect is mild and gradual ("nhẹ và từ từ"). "Lá chỉ hạ pH nhẹ và từ từ, trông chờ pH tụt mạnh là sai." is cut from the magazine's later list, so the pH effect is said once; "trông chờ … là sai" is in no fact (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

These are cut, each a claim one site gives plain, two sites' words joined, or a thing said twice (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026, on the first reader's fact points): "Một lớp lá khô dưới đáy làm nước ngả vàng nâu nhạt." (fact 10, one site; the yellow tint of facts 41, 53 and 54 is lá bàng's alone, and beech stains only slightly, fact 14) / "Người nuôi còn dùng trái thông alder (Alnus glutinosa) để hạ pH." ("trái thông alder" is the shop's word, kept only in the shop's item; fact 90's pH use is the magazine's alone) / "Thả quá nhiều lá thì nước ngả nâu đậm." and "Gặp vậy thì vớt bớt lá ra và thay nước." (fact 27 says brown; "very dark brown" and the water change are the shop's, fact 33) / ", và dùng lá trong nước cứng là sai" from the magazine's hard-water item, which keeps fact 8's "Cách tự nhiên không làm chua được nước cứng." (no fact says using leaves in hard water is wrong).

These are written word for word, each in place of the draft's sentence or item named (the facts' own words; the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026): "Vi khuẩn và nấm phân hủy lá và tạo ra chất nhầy mà cá bột gặm." in place of "Vi khuẩn và nấm phân hủy lá, phủ lên lá một lớp màng sinh học nhầy, và cá bột gặm lớp màng này." (fact 6: a slime, not a biofilm, which is fact 7's own word) / "Tạp chí này kể tên các cá cho bể lót lá khô, trong đó có Betta hoang dã, Apistogramma, Badis, cá đĩa và cá Uaru fernandezyepezi." (fact 39's "include"; no "hợp"; the magazine is named in the sentence before it, and its two pages are one site) / in the shop's list: "Lá ổi khô cứng hơn phần lớn các lá, tan chậm nên nhả tanin từ từ." (fact 77), "Lá cọ khô (hay lá dừa khô) là lá cứng, phân hủy trong nước chậm hơn phần lớn lá khác." (fact 80), "Lá nhãn khô được mô tả là không độc, cứng và lâu mục trong nước." (fact 82), "Lá xoài khô được liệt kê là dùng được trong bể thủy sinh có cây." (fact 84) / under the shop's credit, as its own sentence right after "… cho 20 lít.", word for word, its credit inside it: "Nếu nước ngả nâu rất đậm thì tiệm khuyên vớt lá ra và thay 10–15% nước." (fact 33, its amount kept; the fact check reads a sentence of its own after a credited one as uncredited) / the plain "Theo dõi pH sau khi thả lá." and the plain step "Lá còn nổi thì có thể chặn cho lá nằm xuống đáy." become one step, the last of "Nên làm gì", under the magazine's credit, word for word: "Tạp chí này ghi: chặn cho lá nằm xuống đáy, và theo dõi pH cho tới khi pH ổn định." (fact 21, the magazine's alone: the other sinking facts are lá bàng's, or say most leaves sink by themselves; one opening for the magazine's claims in a row; a step to do never sits under the mistakes heading, where a reader takes it as a mistake: the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

Each credit's claims stay together: the shop's (aquasetup's two pages) in one block, its list of other leaves, its "không dùng lá đang phân hủy" and first-leaf amount, and its very-dark-brown step; the magazine's two pages in one block after it. Two facts the rules reader took for one site's have two: boiling sterilises leaves but drives off the beneficial compounds (fact 26, seriouslyfish and the magazine) and activated carbon removes the tannin (fact 31, Seachem and the shop): both stand plain (the Glossary lead, Fri 20 Nov 2026, on the first reader's read).

These are written word for word, each in place of the draft's sentence or opening named (the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026 evening batch, with the chief of staff's rulings): "Tạp chí này cũng ghi:" in place of "Một bài tạp chí khác ghi:" / "Luộc lá thì khử trùng được lá, nhưng làm mất các chất có lợi." in place of "Luộc lá trước khi thả làm lá mất các chất có lợi." / "KH cao làm tác dụng hạ pH mất nhanh. Vì vậy, tạp chí khuyên làm mềm nước trước. Lá hợp nhất với nước mềm tự nhiên hoặc nước RO." in place of "KH cao làm tác dụng hạ pH mất nhanh, nên làm mềm nước trước. Lá hợp nhất với nước mềm tự nhiên hoặc nước RO." / "Để lá khô hẳn, chẳng hạn trong nhà kho, rồi cất ở chỗ khô ráo." in place of "Phơi lá thật khô.". The boiling sentence stands plain (two sites). The meaning's "cây thủy sinh" stands (the Writing Lead).

The heading "Sai lầm hay gặp" becomes "Sai lầm cần tránh" (the Writing Lead, by the heading rule: no fact says these mistakes are common). Its items stay under it as they are, but for those named in these lines.
Each sentence and item not named in these lines stays word for word where the draft has it.
free: Khi mục, lá nhả tanin làm pH hạ, và lớp lá là chỗ cá bột kiếm ăn.
Một lớp lá khô dưới đáy làm nước ngả vàng nâu nhạt.
Vi khuẩn và nấm phân hủy lá, phủ lên lá một lớp màng sinh học nhầy, và cá bột gặm lớp màng này.
Một bài tạp chí kể tên những cá hợp với bể lót lá khô: Betta hoang dã, Apistogramma, Badis, cá đĩa và cá Uaru fernandezyepezi.
Người nuôi còn dùng trái thông alder (Alnus glutinosa) để hạ pH.
Lá ổi khô cứng hơn hầu hết các lá, tan chậm nên nhả tanin từ từ.
Lá cọ khô (lá dừa khô) là lá cứng, phân hủy trong nước chậm hơn đa số lá khác.
Lá nhãn khô không độc, cứng và lâu mục trong nước.
Lá xoài khô dùng được trong bể thủy sinh có cây.
Theo dõi pH sau khi thả lá.
Thả quá nhiều lá thì nước ngả nâu đậm.
Gặp vậy thì vớt bớt lá ra và thay nước.
Lá chỉ hạ pH nhẹ và từ từ, trông chờ pH tụt mạnh là sai.
Cách tự nhiên không làm chua được nước cứng, và dùng lá trong nước cứng là sai.
Một bài tạp chí khác ghi:
Luộc lá trước khi thả làm lá mất các chất có lợi.
KH cao làm tác dụng hạ pH mất nhanh, nên làm mềm nước trước. Lá hợp nhất với nước mềm tự nhiên hoặc nước RO.
Phơi lá thật khô.
Sai lầm hay gặp
Sau khi thả lá, theo dõi pH cho tới khi pH ổn định.
Nếu nước ngả nâu rất đậm thì tiệm khuyên vớt lá ra và thay 10–15% nước.
Một bài tạp chí kể tên các cá cho bể lót lá khô, trong đó có Betta hoang dã, Apistogramma, Badis, cá đĩa và cá Uaru fernandezyepezi.
Lá còn nổi thì có thể chặn cho lá nằm xuống đáy.

Where a fact limits the claim, the limit is said beside it; if it isn't, the claim takes the credit of the site that gives it broadly. A claim only one site gives takes that site's credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A Vietnamese word that plainly translates another site's word for a thing is the thing's name and needs no credit. A word that is not a plain translation, or a trade name only one shop uses, stays that shop's word, under its credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Each thing is named as its fact names it. A substance, product or tool never takes the name of another, even one keepers use in its place (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A plain sentence says only what two sites give. A part that only one site gives goes in its own sentence under that site's credit, never joined to the two-site part in one sentence (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A word the entry uses for one thing (a name, a shape, a sign) is never used in it for another. Where two things share a fact's word, the second gets a plain word of its own (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).
A name in brackets under a page's credit is that page's own word for the thing, or it isn't there (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A sentence that only sends the reader to the site's own entry or tool is no claim and needs no outside source. Each source's claims are kept together where the order allows. A source named again is "tiệm này", "hội này" or "nguồn người nuôi này" while it is the last of its kind named. write: What CO2 does for plants and for fish only as the facts give it, each amount with its unit, saying whose it is when one page gives it (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

Each way of adding CO2 by the name Vietnamese shops write, with its own facts and cautions. What one way does is never said of another (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
How a level is checked only as facts give it. pH's entry is linked, and KH's where a fact ties them (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
Its danger to fish, and when a source says to turn it off, only as facts give them (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
Oxy hòa tan's and Sục khí's entries are linked where a fact ties them (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).
The entry writes "CO2", as the site does. "bình CO2" is the site's word for the cylinder (the Glossary lead's line; the Writing Lead's yes, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

A product sold as "carbon lỏng", "CO2 lỏng" or "CO2 nước" is said as its fact names it, and never said to add CO2 unless a fact says so (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026).

A figure keeps its own place: a figure a page measured in one country or climate (a Singapore shop's thaw time, a humid-tropics vitamin loss) is said of that place, or of the climate the page names, never of Vietnam unless a fact names Vietnam (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

No "vì", "nên", "do", "để" or "khiến" joins two facts that no single fact joins: two facts side by side stay two sentences, or are joined with "và" (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A claim only one page makes (one keeper's blog, one shop, a news report) says whose it is ("Một tiệm ghi …", "Một tiệm ở Singapore ghi …", "Một nguồn người nuôi ghi …", "Một bài báo nói …"), with the shop's or keeper's place in those same words when the fact gives it; one such opening can carry several claims of the same page, and a claim two pages make needs none. It is never written as plain fact. A dose or amount several times the entry's main one is left out, or named as the stronger one it is (the chief of staff, Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Every number carries its unit as its fact gives it; a figure whose fact gives no unit (such as a page's "KH 4–5") is left out, or said in the fact's own words ("nước cứng, đệm tốt") (the chief of staff, Tue 17 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

An entry names at most three pages this way and doesn't grow to carry more. Past three, it drops the one-page claims a keeper can't act on (why a thing happens, lists of possible causes, background); a one-page claim a keeper acts on (a dose, a time, a step, a warning) waits for a second page from research; what is still over is left out. An entry may come out shorter than its length rather than pad (the chief of staff, Tue 17 and Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

When two or more claims in a row are one page's, they go under one opening, as a list or as one sentence with semicolons, never an opening per sentence; a list under an opening counts as credited, each item included (the chief of staff, Wed 18 Nov 2026: standing line for every term, from Thu 19's first writes).

Two pages of one site are credited apart in neutral words: the first as its facts call it ("Một tiệm ghi:"), the second "Một bài khác ghi:". They are never called another shop and never another page of the same shop, because no fact says whose site a page is. Two different shops keep "Một tiệm ghi:", "Một tiệm khác ghi:", then "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi:" (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A group of fish is named by a name the site has a page for, or by the scientific name its fact writes. Otherwise, where the fact speaks of the whole group, the sentence uses the fact's own word for the group, with no "một số"; where it speaks of some of a group, it says "một số loài" with the fact's widest word. Never "nhiều" or "các loài", which widen the fact (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term, in place of Thu 19's).

A fact's own hedges and amounts stay as it gives them: a hedge is never dropped or added, and an amount is never rounded, widened or narrowed (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Two pages of one site are one source: they count as one toward the three pages an entry names, and a claim only one site's pages give is that site's claim and carries its credit; a claim two sites give stands plain (the chief of staff, Thu 19 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A term's meaning rests on two sites where two define it. Where only one does, it says only what that fact gives and stands without a credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A claim stands plain when two sites carry it: one gives it as broadly as the sentence says it, and another gives the same thing in other words, or for some of the cases it covers. Where a fact limits the claim, the limit is said beside it; if it isn't, the claim takes the credit of the site that gives it broadly. A claim only one site gives takes that site's credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A Vietnamese word that plainly translates another site's word for a thing is the thing's name and needs no credit. A word that is not a plain translation, or a trade name only one shop uses, stays that shop's word, under its credit (the chief of staff's line in the Writing Lead's words, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Each thing is named as its fact names it. A substance, product or tool never takes the name of another, even one keepers use in its place (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A plain sentence says only what two sites give. A part that only one site gives goes in its own sentence under that site's credit, never joined to the two-site part in one sentence (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A word the entry uses for one thing (a name, a shape, a sign) is never used in it for another. Where two things share a fact's word, the second gets a plain word of its own (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).
A name in brackets under a page's credit is that page's own word for the thing, or it isn't there (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A sentence that only sends the reader to the site's own entry or tool is no claim and needs no outside source. It is a pointer and says nothing more: "<what>: xem mục <entry>." or "Kiểm tra <what> bằng <tool> của AquaTome." A sentence that says what a thing is, what it does or which group it is in needs an outside source even when it links the site's page (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

Each source's claims are kept together where the order allows. A source named again is "tiệm này", "hội này" or "nguồn người nuôi này" while it is the last of its kind named. Where it comes back after another of its kind, it is "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai cũng ghi:", as Thu 19's line says. If the second hasn't been introduced yet, it is named by what its page gave or is about ("Tiệm kể các loại tảo ở trên", "Nguồn người nuôi viết về Betta tự cắn đuôi"). "kia", "nói ở trên" and "khác ở trên" are not used (the Writing Lead, through the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A page's kind as research gives it (a shop, a society, a keeper, a paper, a reference) may open its credit; a kind no research gives is not used (the chief of staff, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A heading ends "này". The first sentence under a heading that comes back to a source names it again: "Tiệm thứ nhất / Tiệm thứ hai", or by what its page gave, where two of its kind have been named. "Hội này", "tiệm này" or "nguồn người nuôi này" stay only where a single source of that kind has been named on the page (the Writing Lead, with the chief of staff's yes, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).

A medicine named in an entry by its name (erythromycin, muối hồ cá) carries no amount: no dose, no part of a dose ("nửa liều", "gấp đôi"), no length of a course. Straight after the sentence that names it comes one sentence, which says nothing more: where the site has an open guide on that disease, "Liều và cách dùng: xem bài <the guide's title>."; where it has none, the guide is held or gone, or the medicine is used on something that isn't a fish disease (algae, say), "Liều và cách dùng: theo nhãn thuốc." A line that sends the reader to treatment without naming a medicine is a pointer: "Cách chữa <the disease>: xem bài <the guide's title>." Neither ever points to "bài hướng dẫn chữa bệnh", which is no page, nor to the guides list. Until a guide's link is in, its title stands as plain words (the Writing Lead, with the chief of staff's yes and rider, Fri 20 Nov 2026: standing line for every term).
